<a id="r017-reflection-tuning-data-recycling-improves-llm-instruction-tuning"></a>
## Reflection-Tuning: Data Recycling Improves LLM Instruction-Tuning

**ID:** R017  **Category:** E (Parametric / learned reflection (training-based))  **Authors:** Li et al.  **Venue:** NeurIPS 2023 wksp / arXiv  **Learning locus:** gradient_weight_update  **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.11716

### Basic info

- **name**: Reflection-Tuning: Data Recycling Improves LLM Instruction-Tuning

- **year**: 2023

- **authors**: Ming Li, Lichang Chen, Jiuhai Chen, Shwai He, Heng Huang, Jiuxiang Gu, Tianyi Zhou (University of Maryland; Adobe Research). Lead author Ming Li et al.

- **venue**: NeurIPS 2023 Workshop on Instruction Tuning and Instruction Following; arXiv preprint (arXiv:2310.11716)

- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.11716

- **code url**: https://github.com/tianyi-lab/Reflection_Tuning (also mirrored at https://github.com/MingLiiii/Reflection_Tuning)


### Core mechanism

- **reflection type**:

> learned-critic-model / verbal-self-critique applied to training data: an oracle LLM (ChatGPT/GPT) acts as a judge that introspects on each instruction-response pair against explicit criteria and rewrites it. The reflection is then distilled into the SFT set via gradient training, so the locus of learning is a weight update of the student model rather than the reflection being verbal-only at inference.

- **feedback source**:

> self-generated by an oracle/teacher LLM (ChatGPT) acting as judge against fixed, human-specified criteria; no external tool, unit-test, environment reward, or human label is used to produce the recycled data. Evaluation uses GPT-4/ChatGPT as judge (LLM-as-a-judge).

- **iteration structure**:

> single-shot two-phase recycling per data point (instruction-reflection phase followed by response-reflection phase); each phase is one reflect-then-regenerate pass over the original pair. Not iterative-refine or search; the whole recycled dataset is then used for standard SFT.

- **reflection object**:

> instruction-tuning training data (both the instruction text x and the response text y of each pair are reflected on and rewritten). The reflection is ultimately distilled into the student model's weights through supervised fine-tuning on the recycled data, so the modified artifacts are output content (instruction+response pairs) which then become model weights.


### Learning paradigm

- **learning locus**: gradient_weight_update

- **requires training**: SFT (supervised instruction tuning of the student model on the oracle-recycled data; the recycling step itself is training-free / prompting only)

- **reward or critic model**:

> self-as-judge / oracle-LLM-as-judge: ChatGPT is prompted as an oracle 'critic' to score and rewrite data against criteria such as Complexity of Topic, Level of Detail, Knowledge Required, Ambiguity, Logical Reasoning (for instructions) and Helpfulness, Relevance, Accuracy, Level of Details (for responses). No separately trained reward model and no verifiable reward.

- **distillation target**:

> model-weights: the oracle's reflection is materialized as a higher-quality recycled SFT dataset and then distilled into the student model's parameters via fine-tuning. Intermediate artifact is improved prompt/response data, but the persistent learned artifact is weights.

- **emergent vs engineered**:

> engineered: the reflective behavior is fully prompt/scaffold-engineered. Human-specified criteria are inserted into the oracle prompt as a chain-of-thought guide (inspired by CoT/ToT) to elicit diverse critical responses; the reflection is not an RL-emergent capability.


### Memory mechanism

- **memory type**: none (no persistent agent memory). The only 'memory' is the recycled static SFT dataset; there is no episodic memory, scratchpad, or skill library used at inference.

- **memory persistence**: cross-task in the weak sense that knowledge from recycled data is baked into weights and applies to all downstream instructions; there is no explicit episodic/cross-session memory store.

- **memory curation mechanism**: n/a — the method has no growing memory to curate. Data is recycled once (the original dataset size is preserved, e.g. 52,002 Alpaca samples or 70k WizardLM samples are rewritten one-to-one, not accumulated).


### Reflection granularity & timing

- **error localization granularity**:

> response-level / holistic: the oracle reflects on and rewrites a whole instruction or whole response against coarse criteria, rather than localizing a specific failing token, step, or reasoning sub-step. No step-level or token-level error attribution.

- **intra task vs inter task**:

> inter-task in effect: improvement is achieved by reflecting on a corpus of independent training examples and transferring the gains into model weights that generalize across tasks; it is not within-one-task iterative refinement of a single query at test time.

- **failure recovery vs avoidance**: post-hoc-revision: the oracle revises (recycles) already-collected suboptimal data before training. There is no mid-trajectory recovery and no per-episode retry at inference; quality issues are addressed offline.


### Application domain

- **task domains**:

> general instruction following / general-alignment (open-ended instruction tuning). Evaluated on instruction-following quality plus general QA/reasoning and commonsense benchmarks; not focused on code, math, web-navigation, or embodied tasks.

- **benchmarks**:

> AlpacaEval (AlpacaFarm) leaderboard; Vicuna test set (pair-wise GPT-4 judged); Huggingface Open LLM Leaderboard = ARC (25-shot), HellaSwag (10-shot), MMLU, TruthfulQA; data-quality metrics include IFD score (from Cherry LLM) and Sentence-BERT coherence.


### Evaluation results

- **headline result**:

> On Llama2-7B: Recycled WizardLM 7B reaches 78.88% and Recycled Alpaca 7B reaches 76.99% win rate on the AlpacaEval leaderboard (vs Davinci003, GPT-4 judge), beating the original Alpaca 7B (26.46%), original WizardLM 7B and Vicuna 7B v1.3 (76.84%); on the Vicuna test set the recycled Alpaca wins 88.75% and recycled WizardLM 81.25% (GPT-4 judge), all with the same data count and model size.

- **baselines**:

> Models trained on the original (un-recycled) datasets: Alpaca 7B, WizardLM 7B, plus comparison models Vicuna 7B v1.3, LLaMA2-Chat 7B, WizardLM 13B, Guanaco 7B/33B/65B, Baize-v2 13B, airoboros 65B, Xwin-LM 7B, and SelFee (which also uses oracle-based response refinement but more data and no instruction enhancement).

- **gains vs baseline**:

> AlpacaEval win rate: Recycled Alpaca 7B 76.99% vs original Alpaca 7B 26.46% (+50.5 points), and exceeds Vicuna 7B v1.3 (76.84%) and WizardLM 13B (75.31%) despite same/smaller data and size. Open LLM Leaderboard average: Recycled Alpaca 7B 56.18 vs original Alpaca 7B 50.21 (+5.97); Recycled WizardLM 7B 56.21 vs original WizardLM 7B 54.18 (+2.03); both comparable to LLaMA2-Chat 7B (56.34) which uses extra RLHF. 13B: Recycled Alpaca 13B reaches 83.42% AlpacaEval win rate and 58.93 Open LLM avg with only 52k recycled samples.

- **compute cost profile**:

> Recycling cost = two oracle (ChatGPT) API passes per training example (one instruction-reflection pass + one response-reflection pass), each pass with criteria-based CoT, over the whole base dataset (e.g. 52,002 Alpaca / 70k WizardLM pairs); no extra training of the oracle. Student training cost is identical to a standard SFT run (3 epochs, batch 128, lr 2e-5, max len 2048) on the same number of examples. Inference cost of the resulting model is single-pass (no test-time reflection overhead), so all added cost is one-time offline data-recycling API calls.


### Limitations & critique

- **known limitations**:

> Reflection quality is bounded by the oracle LLM (ChatGPT) and the fixed human-chosen criteria; recycled responses become substantially longer (e.g. Alpaca response length 65.5 -> 377.2 tokens), confounding length-sensitive win-rate judges. Evaluation relies heavily on LLM-as-a-judge (GPT-4/ChatGPT) with known positional/length biases. No mechanism filters whether a rewrite actually helps the specific student model (addressed later by the Selective Reflection-Tuning follow-up). Limited to instruction-following / general benchmarks; not validated on code, math, agentic, or safety-critical tasks.

- **oracle or external feedback dependency**:

> oracle-LLM dependency: the entire improvement signal comes from a stronger oracle/teacher model (ChatGPT) introspecting and rewriting data. There is no ground-truth label, no external verifier/tool, and no environment reward; it is distillation-from-a-better-judge rather than label-free intrinsic self-correction, so gains depend on the oracle being more capable than the base data source.

- **self correction efficacy**:

> net-positive but oracle-dependent: recycling consistently improves instruction-following and benchmark averages, but the 'self-correction' is teacher-model reflection injected into training data rather than a model correcting itself at inference; gains are contingent on the oracle's superior judgment, not on intrinsic self-verification of the base model.

- **calibration effect**: not-measured: the paper does not report calibration or confidence/overconfidence ('reasoning tax') metrics; it measures win rates, accuracy benchmarks, perplexity, coherence, and IFD, but not calibration.


### Failure analysis

- **failure attribution capability**: n/a — this is a data-improvement / instruction-tuning method, not a failure-attribution or error-localization system; it does not classify failure modes or attribute responsible agents/steps.

- **failure mode addressed**:

> Targets low-quality / suboptimal instruction-tuning data (noisy, overly simple, or misaligned instruction-response pairs that degrade instruction tuning). Loosely maps to 'superficial / low-quality supervision' rather than any specific MAST multi-agent failure mode; addresses weak instruction complexity, poor instruction-response coherence, and shallow responses.

- **dataset or benchmark released**:

> Yes — recycled datasets (Recycled Alpaca, Recycled WizardLM) and trained Recycled models plus code released at https://github.com/tianyi-lab/Reflection_Tuning. No new evaluation benchmark introduced (uses existing AlpacaEval / Open LLM Leaderboard / Vicuna sets).


### Relations

- **builds on**:

> Alpaca (Taori et al., 2023) and WizardLM/Evol-Instruct (Xu et al., 2023) as base datasets; AlpaGasus (Chen et al., 2023) and Cherry LLM / IFD score (Li et al., 2023) for data-quality selection; Self-Instruct (Wang et al., 2023); 'LLMs can self-improve' (Huang et al., 2022); Constitutional AI / RLAIF self-alignment (Bai et al., 2022; Lee et al., 2023); SelFee (Ye et al., 2023) self-feedback revision; Chain-of-Thought and Tree-of-Thoughts prompting (Wei et al.; Yao et al.); LLM-as-a-judge / MT-Bench (Zheng et al., 2023).

- **extended by or inspired**:

> Direct successor by the same group: Selective Reflection-Tuning: Student-Selected Data Recycling for LLM Instruction-Tuning (Li et al., ACL 2024 Findings, arXiv:2402.10110), which adds a student model that accepts/rejects each oracle rewrite using IFD and a new r-IFD metric for sample-efficient, student-compatible recycling. More broadly cited within the LLM instruction-data-quality / data-synthesis and self-alignment literature.

- **citation count**: 32 (Semantic Scholar, as of June 2026); the ACL 2024 follow-up 'Selective Reflection-Tuning' has ~85 citations.


### Other / reserved fields

- **reasoning model native**: no — predates and does not target o1/R1-style reasoning models with built-in reflection; it engineers reflection externally via an oracle LLM over training data on Llama2-7B/13B.

- **on policy distillation link**:

> Related to off-policy distillation rather than on-policy distillation: an oracle/teacher reflects and rewrites data, then the student is SFT-trained on that fixed teacher-generated data (off-policy, teacher-on-policy). The follow-up Selective Reflection-Tuning moves toward student-aware (more on-policy-flavored) selection by letting the student accept/reject rewrites via IFD/r-IFD, foreshadowing on-policy-distillation / skill-compatibility ideas.

- **sample efficiency**:

> High in data-count terms: one-to-one recycling preserves dataset size while improving quality (e.g. Recycled Alpaca 13B reaches 83.42% AlpacaEval win rate with only ~52k recycled samples, and recycled 7B models beat 13B/33B/65B baselines trained on far more data). Each example requires two oracle API passes; the follow-up explicitly emphasizes sample-efficient instruction tuning.


---

<a id="r024-selfee-iterative-self-revising-llm-empowered-by-self-feedback-generation"></a>
## SelFee: Iterative Self-Revising LLM Empowered by Self-Feedback Generation

**ID:** R024  **Category:** E (Parametric / learned reflection (training-based))  **Authors:** Ye et al.  **Venue:** Blog post + code release (KAIST), 2023; not a formal venue  **Learning locus:** gradient_weight_update  **URL:** https://kaistai.github.io/SelFee/

### Basic info

- **name**: SelFee: Iterative Self-Revising LLM Empowered by Self-Feedback Generation

- **year**: 2023

- **authors**: Seonghyeon Ye*, Yongrae Jo*, Doyoung Kim*, Sungdong Kim, Hyeonbin Hwang, Minjoon Seo (KAIST AI; LK Lab / KAIST)

- **venue**: Blog post + code/model release (KAIST), May 31, 2023; not a formal peer-reviewed venue (no arXiv paper)

- **paper url**: https://kaistai.github.io/SelFee/

- **code url**: https://github.com/kaistAI/SelFee (model diff weights: kaist-ai/selfee-7b-delta, kaist-ai/selfee-13b-delta; training data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/kaist-ai/selfee-train)


### Core mechanism

- **reflection type**:

> verbal-self-critique (model generates its own natural-language feedback and self-revises; the self-critique-and-revise capability is distilled into the model via supervised fine-tuning, i.e. a learned self-feedback generator rather than a separate learned critic model)

- **feedback source**:

> self-generated (the fine-tuned model produces its own feedback sequences with no external tools/retrieval/oracle at inference time). NOTE: the SFT training data was distilled from ChatGPT, and for the Math/Code/Flan portions ChatGPT generated feedback while conditioned on the available ground-truth answers; at inference time SelFee uses no ground truth.

- **iteration structure**:

> iterative-refine (autoregressive answer -> feedback -> revised answer -> feedback ... chain), but the entire iterative loop is emitted within a single forward pass / single inference; model autonomously decides when to stop ('Revision is not needed.') or can be forced to a minimum number of revisions

- **reflection object**:

> output content (the model's own answer to an instruction) via an interleaved natural-language reasoning/feedback chain; the revision target is the response text, not a reasoning chain over an environment, action trajectory, or external memory


### Learning paradigm

- **learning locus**:

> gradient_weight_update (the self-feedback + self-revision behavior is baked into the LLaMA weights via supervised fine-tuning on 178K ChatGPT-distilled feedback+revision instances; at inference there is no weight update, the iterative refinement is purely generated)

- **requires training**: SFT (supervised fine-tuning of LLaMA 7B/13B on 178K instruction->answer+feedback-chain+revision sequences; 3 epochs, lr 2e-5, global batch 128, max length 2048, via FastChat). No RL or preference optimization.

- **reward or critic model**:

> self-as-judge baked into the model: the same model generates its own feedback used to drive revisions. Training supervision is knowledge distilled from ChatGPT (teacher LLM) as feedback/revision generator; no separately trained reward model and no verifiable reward at inference.

- **distillation target**:

> model-weights (ChatGPT-generated self-feedback-and-revision trajectories are distilled into the LLaMA model parameters so the student can self-feedback and self-revise without the teacher, tools, retrieval, or in-context demonstrations)

- **emergent vs engineered**:

> engineered: the reflective self-feedback/self-revision behavior is induced by supervised fine-tuning on explicitly constructed feedback+revision chains (teacher distillation), not RL-emergent. The data-generation scaffold (ChatGPT generates answer, then feedback, then conditional revision) is prompt/scaffold-engineered; the resulting behavior is then internalized in weights.


### Memory mechanism

- **memory type**: short-term/scratchpad (the feedback+revision chain functions as an in-context scratchpad within a single inference); no persistent episodic memory, skill library, or external store

- **memory persistence**:

> within-episode (the feedback/revision chain exists only within the single inference for one instruction; nothing persists across queries). The 'learning' that persists across tasks lives in the fine-tuned weights, not in a memory module.

- **memory curation mechanism**:

> n/a (no explicit memory store to curate; the model autonomously truncates the revision chain when feedback signals 'Revision is not needed.' or a max-iteration cap is hit, but this is generation termination, not memory curation)


### Reflection granularity & timing

- **error localization granularity**: response-level (feedback critiques and revises the whole answer/response holistically and assigns a quality score; not step-level, token-level, or block-level localization)

- **intra task vs inter task**: intra-task at inference (refines a single answer within one task via the feedback/revision chain). Cross-task generalization comes from the SFT weights rather than from transferred experience artifacts.

- **failure recovery vs avoidance**: post-hoc-revision (the model produces an initial answer then critiques and revises it within the same inference); it is in-flight self-revision of output content rather than retry-with-reset across episodes


### Application domain

- **task domains**: general instruction-following / open-ended generation (creative writing, long-form text), with training data also spanning math, code, QA/reasoning (Flan); evaluated primarily as a general chat assistant

- **benchmarks**:

> Vicuna evaluation setting (80 diverse queries, GPT-4-as-judge with bidirectional/position-debiased scoring, relative to ChatGPT). Training data sourced from Stanford Alpaca, AQUA/GSM8K/MATH, Conala/DeepMind Code Contest/DrRepair/MBPP, FLAN collection, ShareGPT.


### Evaluation results

- **headline result**:

> On the Vicuna 80-query GPT-4 evaluation (relative score vs ChatGPT=100), SelFee 7B/13B outperform LLaMA, Alpaca, Vicuna, and Guanaco and are roughly comparable to ChatGPT. SelFee-13B with >=3 enforced revisions scores 101.4 vs ChatGPT; SelFee-13B with no enforced revisions scores 98.2. Notably a 7B model with >=3 revisions (101.4) beats a 13B model with no enforced revisions (98.2).

- **baselines**:

> LLaMA, Stanford Alpaca, Vicuna, Guanaco (open-source LLaMA-based instruction models), and ChatGPT (closed teacher model, used as the 100-point reference); also internal ablation across SelFee variants with different minimum required revisions

- **gains vs baseline**:

> Versus the strongest open-source baseline (Vicuna), SelFee is reported to win on the Vicuna setting and reach near-ChatGPT relative scores. Key reported delta is internal: enforcing a minimum of 3 revisions on SelFee-13B raises the relative score to 101.4 vs 98.2 with no enforced revisions (~+3.2 points), and the 7B@3-revisions matches/beats 13B@0-revisions (101.4 vs 98.2), supporting the inference-compute-scaling claim. Exact per-baseline numeric deltas beyond these are presented as win-rate bar charts rather than tabulated numbers.

- **compute cost profile**:

> Training: SFT of LLaMA 7B/13B on 178K instances, 3 epochs (one-time cost). Inference: a single forward pass but generates a longer sequence (answer + feedback + multiple revisions), so token/compute cost scales roughly with the number of revisions; enforcing >=3 revisions increases generated tokens vs a single-shot answer. The paper frames this as scaling inference computation (longer generation) being more effective than scaling model size.


### Limitations & critique

- **known limitations**:

> Authors state SelFee (7B/13B) underperforms ChatGPT and lacks knowledge in math, reasoning, factuality, and coding (a common limitation of LLaMA-finetuned models attributed to weak base models, echoing 'The False Promise of Imitating Proprietary LLMs'). Evaluation itself is acknowledged as limited: only 80 queries, GPT-4-judge positional bias, inconsistency and unreliability; authors explicitly say to take claims 'with a grain of salt.' Forcing revisions when unnecessary can degrade quality.

- **oracle or external feedback dependency**:

> intrinsic-only at inference (no external tool/verifier/oracle used when running SelFee). However, the distilled training signal is not purely intrinsic: ChatGPT served as teacher, and for Math/Code/Flan subsets feedback was generated by ChatGPT conditioned on ground-truth answers, so oracle/teacher information leaks into the training data even though inference is intrinsic.

- **self correction efficacy**:

> net-positive in the reported setting: enforcing more revisions (up to 3) improves the Vicuna-setting relative score (98.2 -> 101.4 for 13B), and revision-enabled models beat non-revising larger models. Task-dependent though: gains concentrate in open-ended/creative generation; forcing unnecessary revisions can reduce quality, and the model does not overcome base-model weaknesses on math/reasoning/factuality/coding.

- **calibration effect**: not-measured (no calibration / confidence-accuracy analysis reported; the model emits a self-assessed quality score in feedback but no calibration study is provided)


### Failure analysis

- **failure attribution capability**:

> n/a (SelFee is a self-correction generation method, not a failure-attribution / error-localization study; its feedback assigns a holistic quality score and a revise/no-revise decision rather than attributing failures to specific steps or agents)

- **failure mode addressed**:

> Targets low-quality / under-refined single-shot responses by forcing iterative self-revision; mitigates 'superficial single-pass answers' for open-ended generation. Does not address (and is limited by) base-model knowledge gaps in math, reasoning, factuality, and coding; risk of over-revision (degrading correct answers when revision is forced unnecessarily), loosely related to MAST-style 'superficial self-reflection' / over-correction failure modes.

- **dataset or benchmark released**:

> Yes: the 178K-instance SelFee training dataset of instruction->answer+feedback+revision chains is released (https://huggingface.co/datasets/kaist-ai/selfee-train); also released model diff weights (selfee-7b-delta, selfee-13b-delta), full data-augmentation/training/inference/evaluation code, and inference outputs + GPT-4 review scores. No new evaluation benchmark introduced (reuses the Vicuna 80-query setting).


### Relations

- **builds on**:

> Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023); Self-Refine (Madaan et al., 2023); Self-Correction (Welleck et al., 2022, 'Generating Sequences by Learning to Self-Correct'); RL4F (Akyurek et al., 2023); PEER (Schick et al., 2022); Self-Critiquing / Self-Critique (Saunders et al., 2022). Engineering base: Stanford Alpaca, Vicuna/FastChat, LLaMA; data from Alpaca, AQUA, GSM8K, MATH, Conala, DeepMind Code Contest, DrRepair, MBPP, FLAN collection, ShareGPT; teacher distillation from ChatGPT.

- **extended by or inspired**:

> Cited/positioned as a training-based self-correction baseline in survey/analysis works, e.g. Kamoi et al. (TACL 2024) 'When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction' (notes SelFee trains a model to emulate self-correction); the ICSF self-feedback survey (Liang et al., arXiv:2407.14507); 'A Survey on LLM-as-a-Judge'; and related KAIST follow-ups such as Volcano (Lee et al., NAACL 2024, self-feedback-guided multimodal revision).

- **citation count**:

> ~80 (Google Scholar, per author Yongrae Jo's profile entry 'Selfee: Iterative self-revising llm... Blog post, 2023', as of June 2026). Not indexed with a count on Semantic Scholar because it is a blog post rather than an arXiv/peer-reviewed paper.


### Other / reserved fields

- **reasoning model native**:

> no (predates and does not target o1/R1-style reasoning models with built-in reflection; SelFee instead manufactures reflective behavior in a 2023-era LLaMA via SFT). The single-pass interleaved feedback/revision chain is conceptually a precursor to such models' inline self-correction.

- **on policy distillation link**:

> Off-policy distillation: the student is trained on ChatGPT-generated (teacher-policy) feedback/revision trajectories, i.e. offline SFT on teacher outputs rather than on-policy distillation on the student's own rollouts. Relevant to OPD discussions as a contrasting off-policy 'imitate the teacher's self-correction' approach (and a target of the 'False Promise of Imitating Proprietary LLMs' critique).

- **sample efficiency**:

> Training: 178K SFT instances, 3 epochs (LLaMA 7B/13B). Inference: best reported quality reached at a minimum of ~3 self-revisions per query; beyond 3 enforced revisions does not further help, and forcing revisions when unneeded can hurt.


---

<a id="r026-training-language-models-to-self-correct-via-reinforcement-learning"></a>
## Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning

**ID:** R026  **Category:** E (Parametric / learned reflection (training-based))  **Authors:** Aviral Kumar, Vincent Zhuang et al.  **Venue:** ICLR 2025  **Learning locus:** gradient_weight_update  **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12917

### Basic info

- **name**: Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning

- **year**: 2024

- **authors**: Aviral Kumar, Vincent Zhuang, Rishabh Agarwal, Yi Su, John D. Co-Reyes, Avi Singh et al. (18 authors); lead affiliation Google DeepMind

- **venue**: ICLR 2025 (Oral); first posted as arXiv preprint Sep 2024

- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12917


### Core mechanism

- **reflection type**:

> verbal-self-critique (intrinsic self-correction: the model revises its own prior answer over a second turn using only a fixed self-correction instruction, with no external critic or tool feedback at inference). The corrective behavior itself is instilled via reinforcement learning.

- **feedback source**:

> Two distinct signals must be distinguished. At TRAINING time the improvement signal is an environment/verifiable reward (answer-correctness oracle: final-answer correctness for MATH, unit-test pass for code) computed over self-generated correction traces. At TEST/INFERENCE time there is NO external feedback or reward access; the model self-corrects intrinsically using only a self-generated/in-context self-correction prompt.

- **iteration structure**:

> iterative-refine over a small fixed number of turns (multi-turn, typically 2 attempts: first attempt then a self-correction revision; extended to 3 attempts in the rebuttal/Gemma experiments). Sequential self-correction, not tree/MCTS search.

- **reflection object**:

> output content / reasoning chain (the second-turn revision rewrites the answer and its solution reasoning) AND model weights (the self-correction capability is baked into the policy parameters via RL gradient updates). The reflective behavior is parametric/learned, not just an in-context scaffold.


### Learning paradigm

- **learning locus**: gradient_weight_update

- **requires training**:

> RL (multi-turn online policy gradient, REINFORCE-style / RLOO-class with per-turn instantaneous reward and KL penalty); explicitly NOT SFT (the paper shows SFT/STaR/Pair-SFT variants are insufficient). Two-stage RL training.

- **reward or critic model**:

> verifiable reward (oracle answer-correctness / unit-test pass at training time) plus reward shaping (a reward bonus that amplifies traces flipping incorrect->correct between attempts and penalizes correct->incorrect). No separate trained reward model, no separate critic LLM, no stronger teacher model.

- **distillation target**: model-weights (the self-correction strategy is distilled into the policy's own parameters; no external episodic memory or reusable-skill artifact is produced).

- **emergent vs engineered**:

> RL-emergent under an engineered training recipe: the self-correction behavior is learned/instilled by the multi-turn RL objective (with Stage I initialization + Stage II reward bonus) rather than hand-prompted at inference like Reflexion. The two-stage design and reward shaping are engineered to prevent behavior collapse and distribution mismatch, but the resulting correction policy is acquired through RL, not a fixed scaffold.


### Memory mechanism

- **memory type**: short-term/scratchpad (within a multi-turn episode the model conditions on its own first attempt and the self-correction instruction). No persistent long-term episodic memory or skill library.

- **memory persistence**: within-episode (the prior attempt is available as context only within the current multi-turn rollout; nothing is carried across separate test problems).

- **memory curation mechanism**: n/a (no external memory store; the only persistence is the second-turn prefix within the episode and the learned weights).


### Reflection granularity & timing

- **error localization granularity**:

> holistic/outcome-level / response-level: correction operates on the whole answer based on a scalar outcome correctness signal (final-answer correctness or unit-test pass); there is no step-level or token-level error attribution/localization.

- **intra task vs inter task**:

> intra-task (refinement happens within a single problem's multi-turn episode, similar in spirit to Self-Refine but trained); transfer across tasks is via the learned weights generalizing to new problems, not via stored cross-task experience.

- **failure recovery vs avoidance**: mid-trajectory-recovery / post-hoc-revision within the same episode: the model produces a first attempt and then corrects it in a subsequent turn (intrinsic self-correction), rather than retrying on a fresh episode.


### Application domain

- **task domains**: math reasoning and code generation.

- **benchmarks**:

> MATH (trained on MATH train split, evaluated on the uncontaminated MATH500 test set), HumanEval, MBPP-R (code repair), plus held-out generalization sets Functional MATH and MathOdyssey; additional Gemma 2 (2B) open-model experiments added in the rebuttal/appendix.


### Evaluation results

- **headline result**:

> With Gemini 1.0 Pro and Gemini 1.5 Flash, SCoRe achieves state-of-the-art intrinsic self-correction, improving the base models' self-correction by 15.6% on MATH and 9.1% on HumanEval. On MATH, SCoRe attains a +4.4% positive self-correction delta (Delta(t1,t2)) with Accuracy@t2 of ~23.0%; on code it raises MBPP-R from 47.3% to 60.6% and yields a 12.2% self-correction delta on HumanEval. It is described as the first method to obtain a positive intrinsic self-correction rate.

- **baselines**:

> Base model with self-correction prompting (intrinsic prompting, prior 'Self-Correction is not effective' setting), STaR / REST-EM (filtered SFT on successful correction traces), Pair-SFT (synthetic incorrect->correct repair pairs), single-turn RL ('w/o multi-turn training'), and a single-turn RL on base-model-sampled first attempts variant. Reference points include GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4 gap on MBPP-R.

- **gains vs baseline**:

> On MATH, SCoRe's +4.4% self-correction Delta(t1,t2) vs the strongest comparable SFT baseline Pair-SFT (~1.8% gain over base, and an effective +0.2% delta for single-turn RL on fixed base first-turns); SCoRe improves over base model self-correction by 15.6% (MATH) / 9.1% (HumanEval) and surpasses Pair-SFT by ~10.2% in self-correction gain on MATH. Crucially, prior SFT/prompting methods produce a NEGATIVE or near-zero self-correction delta, whereas SCoRe is net-positive.

- **compute cost profile**:

> Training: multi-turn online RL with self-generated rollouts (two stages of policy-gradient training; no extra teacher/reward-model training). Inference: sequential self-correction adds turns; per the rebuttal each additional sequential turn costs ~2.5x less latency than the first attempt due to prefix caching, giving total latency ~1 + c*(T-1) (c<1) vs fully parallel sampling. Combined with self-consistency, parallel+sequential gives a 10.5% gain vs 7.4% for parallel-only at comparable budget.


### Limitations & critique

- **known limitations**:

> Primary experiments on private Gemini 1.0 Pro / 1.5 Flash models (reproducibility limited; partially addressed with Gemma 2 2B in appendix). Restricted to math and code with verifiable correctness rewards (needs tasks with non-multiple-choice, checkable answers; lack of large public training splits for other domains like physics/chemistry). Trained for a small number of attempts (2, extended to 3); scalability to many turns and joint multi-turn training is open. Some design choices (large vs small KL, reward-shaping sign) are intricate; reviewers noted weak theoretical justification for the claimed generalization benefit of self-correction policies.

- **oracle or external feedback dependency**:

> intrinsic-only at inference (no oracle label, tool, or reward at test time), BUT requires a verifiable/oracle correctness reward during RL training (env-reward over self-generated traces). It removes the test-time oracle dependency that earlier 'effective' self-correction relied on, which is the paper's core claim of genuine intrinsic self-correction.

- **self correction efficacy**:

> net-positive: SCoRe achieves a positive intrinsic self-correction delta (e.g., +4.4% on MATH) without test-time label leakage, in contrast to prior methods (prompting, SFT/STaR, Pair-SFT) which are net-negative or near-zero. Efficacy is established on math/code with verifiable rewards.

- **calibration effect**: not-measured (the paper focuses on accuracy and self-correction deltas / fraction of incorrect->correct vs correct->incorrect flips; it does not report confidence-calibration metrics or a 'reasoning-tax' analysis).


### Failure analysis

- **failure attribution capability**:

> n/a (SCoRe is a self-correction training method, not a failure-attribution/diagnosis tool; it does not classify failure modes or attribute responsible steps/agents). However, the paper diagnoses two failure modes of prior training approaches: distribution mismatch/shift and behavior collapse (minimal-edit non-correction).

- **failure mode addressed**:

> Targets the 'superficial self-reflection' / non-correcting failure mode where models leave answers unchanged or make only minimal edits (behavior collapse), and the distribution-mismatch failure where offline SFT correction data does not match the model's own response distribution. It addresses error-loops/over-conservatism by reward shaping that rewards incorrect->correct flips and penalizes correct->incorrect changes.


### Relations

- **builds on**:

> Findings that LLMs cannot reliably intrinsically self-correct (Huang et al. 2023, 'Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet'); STaR / Expert Iteration / REST-EM self-training (Zelikman et al.; Singh et al. 2023 'Beyond Human Data'); REINFORCE/RLOO-style policy gradient for LLMs (Ahmadian et al. 2024) and PPO/RLHF; process/outcome reward and MATH train/test protocol (Lightman et al. 2023 'Let's Verify Step by Step'); reflection/self-refinement scaffolds (Self-Refine, Reflexion) which it contrasts against; multi-turn RL framing.

- **extended by or inspired**:

> Inspired a wave of RL-based self-correction / self-improvement and self-distillation work in 2025-2026, including self-distilled RLVR and on-policy-distillation methods (e.g., 'Self-Distilled RLVR', 'Reinforcement Learning via Self-Distillation', 'Self-Distillation Zero: Self-Revision Turns Binary Rewards into Dense Supervision', 'Expanding the Capabilities of Reinforcement Learning via Text Feedback'), multi-turn self-correction and reasoning-model self-correction studies, and is widely cited as the reference training-based self-correction method alongside reasoning models (o1/R1-style) that exhibit emergent reflection.

- **citation count**: 409 (Semantic Scholar, mid-2026)


### Other / reserved fields

- **reasoning model native**:

> Not specifically: SCoRe trains general (non-reasoning-specialized) Gemini/Gemma models to self-correct via RL, predating and complementing o1/R1-style reasoning models. It is frequently discussed as a precursor/parallel approach to the emergent reflection seen in o1-style models, and reviewers noted its relevance to o1-like inference-time scaling, but it does not require a reasoning-model substrate.

- **on policy distillation link**:

> Strongly relevant: SCoRe is a canonical on-policy / self-generated-data RL method (training under the model's own distribution of correction traces with REINFORCE-style updates), and it is heavily cited by the 2025-2026 on-policy-distillation (OPD) and self-distilled-RLVR literature as a foundational self-correction-via-self-data approach, even though SCoRe itself is reward-driven RL rather than teacher-logit distillation.

- **sample efficiency**:

> Reported in turns/stages rather than trial counts: two RL stages (Stage I initialization to avoid collapse + Stage II reward-bonus amplification), each over self-generated multi-turn rollouts; effective with as few as 2 self-correction attempts (extended to 3). Exact rollout/gradient-step counts are not given in the public abstract/reviews.


### Uncertain (not determined)

- code_url
- dataset_or_benchmark_released

<a id="r027-selective-reflection-tuning-student-selected-data-recycling-for-llm-instruction-tuning"></a>
## Selective Reflection-Tuning: Student-Selected Data Recycling for LLM Instruction-Tuning

**ID:** R027  **Category:** E (Parametric / learned reflection (training-based))  **Authors:** Ming Li et al.  **Venue:** Findings of ACL 2024  **Learning locus:** gradient_weight_update  **URL:** https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-acl.958/

### Basic info

- **name**: Selective Reflection-Tuning: Student-Selected Data Recycling for LLM Instruction-Tuning

- **year**: 2024

- **authors**: Ming Li, Lichang Chen, Jiuhai Chen, Shwai He, Jiuxiang Gu, Tianyi Zhou (University of Maryland, College Park; Adobe Research). Lead author Ming Li et al.

- **venue**: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024 (Bangkok, Thailand), pages 16189-16211. arXiv preprint arXiv:2402.10110 (submitted 15 Feb 2024, v2 7 Jun 2024). DOI: 10.18653/v1/2024.findings-acl.958

- **paper url**: https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-acl.958/ (arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10110)

- **code url**: https://github.com/tianyi-lab/Reflection_Tuning (shared with the Reflection-Tuning project page; sRecycled datasets/models released)


### Core mechanism

- **reflection type**:

> learned-critic-model / teacher-LLM verbal-self-critique applied to training data, gated by a student-side statistical critic. A teacher LLM (ChatGPT/GPT-4) reflects/introspects on each instruction-response pair against explicit criteria and rewrites it (verbal-self-critique over data), then the student model acts as a non-generative, statistics-based critic that accepts or rejects each rewrite using its own IFD / reversed-IFD (r-IFD) perplexity scores. The accepted reflections are distilled into the student via SFT, so the persistent learning locus is a gradient weight update.

- **feedback source**:

> self-generated by an oracle/teacher LLM (ChatGPT, gpt-3.5-turbo / GPT-4) acting as the reflector against fixed human-specified criteria, plus a student-derived statistical signal (IFD and r-IFD computed from the raw base student model's own perplexities). No external tool, unit test, environment reward, or human label is used to produce the recycled data. Final evaluation uses GPT-4 as judge (LLM-as-a-judge) plus a small human study.

- **iteration structure**:

> single-shot two-phase recycling per data point: (1) Selective Instruction Reflection (teacher reflects+regenerates instruction-response; student keeps the pair with higher IFD via argmax) followed by (2) Selective Response Reflection (teacher reflects+regenerates the response; student keeps the pair with lower r-IFD via argmin). Each phase is one reflect-then-regenerate-then-select pass; no iterative-refine loop, no search, no episodic retry. The selectively recycled dataset is then used for one standard SFT run.

- **reflection object**:

> instruction-tuning training data — both the instruction text x and the response text y of each pair are reflected on (rewritten by the teacher) and then selected (by the student). Intermediate modified artifacts are output content (improved instruction+response pairs); the reflection is ultimately distilled into the student model's weights via supervised fine-tuning, so the persistent reflected/modified object is model weights.


### Learning paradigm

- **learning locus**: gradient_weight_update

- **requires training**:

> SFT (supervised instruction tuning of the student model on the selectively-recycled data; both the teacher reflection step and the student IFD/r-IFD selection step are training-free / prompting-and-statistics only — no extra training of teacher or critic). Llama2-7B/13B fine-tuned with Adam, lr 2e-5 (7B) / 1e-5 (13B), batch 128, 3 epochs, max len 2048, warmup 0.03.

- **reward or critic model**:

> self-as-judge / oracle-LLM-as-reflector for generation, plus a student-internal statistical critic for selection: the improvement signal comes from (a) ChatGPT/GPT-4 introspecting and rewriting data against criteria (Complexity, Detail, Knowledge, Ambiguity, Logical Reasoning for instructions; Helpfulness, Relevance, Accuracy, Level of Detail for responses), and (b) the base student model's own IFD (difficulty) and r-IFD (feasibility) perplexity ratios used to accept/reject each rewrite. No separately trained reward model and no verifiable/programmatic reward.

- **distillation target**:

> model-weights: the teacher's reflection, filtered by the student's selection, is materialized as a higher-quality, student-compatible recycled SFT dataset (sRecycled Alpaca / sRecycled WizardLM) and then distilled into the student model's parameters via fine-tuning. Intermediate artifact is improved prompt/response data, but the persistent learned artifact is weights.

- **emergent vs engineered**:

> engineered: the reflective behavior is fully prompt/scaffold-engineered. The teacher is given human-specified criteria as a chain-of-thought guide (it first generates 'critical responses' z_i per criterion, then regenerates the pair) and the student selection rule (argmax IFD, argmin r-IFD) is hand-designed. It is not an RL-emergent reflection capability.


### Memory mechanism

- **memory type**:

> none (no persistent agent memory). The only 'memory' is the static selectively-recycled SFT dataset; there is no episodic memory, scratchpad, or skill library used at inference. The IFD/r-IFD statistics are transient per-sample selection signals, not a retained memory store.

- **memory persistence**:

> cross-task only in the weak sense that knowledge from recycled data is baked into the student's weights and applies to all downstream instructions; there is no explicit episodic / cross-session memory store. Selection statistics must be recomputed per student model and are not persisted.

- **memory curation mechanism**:

> n/a (no growing memory) — but the method does perform a one-time data curation: each original pair is recycled one-to-one and then student-selected/filtered. Samples that were not response-reflected are discarded for response-distribution consistency, so the curated set is smaller than the base set (e.g. Alpaca 52,002 -> sRecycled 37,114; WizardLM-7B 70,000 -> 46,325). This is selection/filtering of static data, not curation of an accumulating memory.


### Reflection granularity & timing

- **error localization granularity**:

> response-level / holistic: the teacher reflects on and rewrites a whole instruction or whole response against coarse criteria, and the student selects at the whole-sample level via IFD (whole instruction-response pair) and r-IFD (whole response->instruction). No step-level, block-level, or token-level error attribution (later follow-ups like T-SHIRT add token-level Selective-IFD).

- **intra task vs inter task**:

> inter-task in effect: improvement is achieved by reflecting on and selecting a corpus of independent training examples and transferring the gains into model weights that generalize across downstream tasks; it is not within-one-task iterative refinement of a single query at test time.

- **failure recovery vs avoidance**:

> post-hoc-revision: the teacher revises (recycles) already-collected suboptimal data and the student filters it before training. There is no mid-trajectory recovery and no per-episode retry at inference; data-quality/compatibility issues are addressed offline.


### Application domain

- **task domains**:

> general instruction following / general-alignment (open-ended instruction tuning). Evaluated on instruction-following quality plus general QA/reasoning and commonsense benchmarks; not focused on code, math, web-navigation, embodied, or tool-use tasks.

- **benchmarks**:

> AlpacaEval Leaderboard (GPT-4 judge vs Davinci003); Pair-wise Comparison (GPT-4 judge vs open-source models); Huggingface Open LLM Leaderboard = ARC (25-shot), HellaSwag (10-shot), MMLU (5-shot), TruthfulQA; MT-Bench (1-turn/2-turn/overall); plus a 108-instruction human study. Data-quality selection uses IFD and the new reversed-IFD (r-IFD); coherence baseline uses Sentence-BERT.


### Evaluation results

- **headline result**:

> On Llama2-7B, with only selectively-recycled data and no RLHF/RLAIF, sRecycled WizardLM 7B reaches 83.48% AlpacaEval win rate (46,325 samples) and sRecycled Alpaca 7B reaches 79.58% (37,114 samples), beating the prior Recycled WizardLM 7B (78.88%, 70k) and Recycled Alpaca 7B (76.99%, 52k) and matching/exceeding much larger models (e.g. Humpback LLaMa 65B 83.71%, Vicuna 13B v1.3 82.11%); sRecycled WizardLM 13B reaches 85.96% (46,064 samples). Open LLM Leaderboard avg: sRecycled WizardLM 7B 56.79, sRecycled Alpaca 7B 56.05. Strikingly, sRecycled WizardLM 7B with only 926 samples (2%) already hits 74.29% AlpacaEval and 57.80 Open LLM avg, beating LIMA.

- **baselines**:

> Prior data-recycling without selection: Recycled WizardLM 7B / Recycled Alpaca 7B (Reflection-Tuning, teacher-only). Reflection ablations: Reflect-on-Instruction only, Reflect-on-Response only, Reflect-on-Ins.+Res. (=Recycled, no selection). Selection ablations: Select-by-Randomness, Select-by-Coherence (Sentence-BERT), Select-by-Perplexity, Select-by-IFD-only, Select-by-r-IFD-only. External models: original Alpaca 7B (26.46%), WizardLM 7B/13B, Vicuna 7B/13B v1.1/v1.3/v1.5, LLaMA2-Chat 7B/13B (RLHF), Zephyr 7B (RLAIF), Humpback 65B, UltraLM 13B, Guanaco 65B, OpenChat V2 13B, Claude2-Alpaca 13B, LIMA 7B, Orca 2 7B, GPT-4/ChatGPT/GPT-3.5/Claude 2.

- **gains vs baseline**:

> Vs the strongest comparable baseline (prior teacher-only Recycled models on the SAME base data): on AlpacaEval, sRecycled WizardLM 7B 83.48% vs Recycled WizardLM 7B 78.88% (+4.6 points) while using LESS data (46,325 vs 70,000); sRecycled Alpaca 7B 79.58% vs Recycled Alpaca 7B 76.99% (+2.59 points) with 37,114 vs 52,002 samples. In the pair-wise GPT-4 ablation (Table 4, win rate metric = (Win-Lose)/All + 1, where 1.0 = tie), sRecycled WizardLM 7B beats original WizardLM 1.560, Reflect-on-Ins.+Res. 1.069, Select-by-IFD-only 1.023, Select-by-r-IFD-only 1.119, Select-by-Perplexity 1.041, Select-by-Coherence 1.128, Select-by-Randomness 1.174. Human study vs original WizardLM 7B: 57 wins / 23 ties / 28 losses (out of 108). vs original Alpaca 7B on AlpacaEval: 79.58% vs 26.46% (+53.1 points).

- **compute cost profile**:

> Recycling cost = two teacher (ChatGPT/GPT-4) API passes per training example (one selective-instruction-reflection pass + one selective-response-reflection pass), each with criteria-based CoT, over the base dataset (52,002 Alpaca / 70,000 WizardLM-7B pairs). Selection adds cheap forward passes on the base student model to compute IFD and r-IFD per candidate (no gradients, no extra model training). Student SFT cost is one standard run (3 epochs, batch 128, lr 2e-5 7B / 1e-5 13B, max len 2048) on FEWER examples than the original set (37,114 / 46,325 after filtering), and as little as 926 samples (2%) for near-peak benchmark scores -> markedly cheaper training. Resulting model inference is single-pass (no test-time reflection overhead). Main added cost is one-time offline teacher API calls; limitation: IFD/r-IFD must be recomputed for each new student model.


### Limitations & critique

- **known limitations**:

> Stated limitation: IFD and r-IFD are student-model-specific, so the selection statistics must be recomputed for every different student model (the selected subset differs per student), which the authors note is still not efficient enough despite being cheaper than generation-based selection. Reflection quality is bounded by the teacher LLM (ChatGPT/GPT-4) and the fixed human-chosen criteria. Recycled responses tend to be longer (avg length up to ~1583 tokens), which can confound length-sensitive GPT-4 win-rate judges. Evaluation relies heavily on LLM-as-a-judge with known positional/length biases. MT-Bench 2-turn score is weak (training used only 1-turn data; e.g. sRecycled Wiz 7B 2-turn 4.588). Scope limited to general instruction following; not validated on code, math, agentic, multi-turn, or safety-critical tasks.

- **oracle or external feedback dependency**:

> external-tool/teacher dependency (no ground-truth oracle): the generative improvement signal comes from a stronger teacher/oracle LLM (ChatGPT/GPT-4) introspecting and rewriting data, while the acceptance signal is the student's own IFD/r-IFD perplexity statistics (intrinsic, label-free). There is no ground-truth label, programmatic verifier, or environment reward; gains are distillation-from-a-better-teacher gated by student-compatibility statistics, so they depend on the teacher being more capable than the base data source.

- **self correction efficacy**:

> net-positive but teacher-dependent: selective recycling consistently improves instruction-following win rates and benchmark averages over both the un-recycled base data and the prior teacher-only Recycled baseline, and the ablations show the random/coherence selection can even harm performance (blind data mixing hurts) — so the student-side IFD/r-IFD selection is the load-bearing component. The 'self-correction' is teacher reflection injected into training data plus student statistical filtering, not a model correcting itself at inference; gains are contingent on the teacher's superior judgment, not on intrinsic self-verification of the base model alone.

- **calibration effect**:

> not-measured: the paper does not report confidence calibration or overconfidence ('reasoning tax') metrics. It measures win rates (AlpacaEval, pair-wise, MT-Bench), accuracy benchmarks (ARC/HellaSwag/MMLU/TruthfulQA), IFD/r-IFD statistics, and a human study, but not calibration.


### Failure analysis

- **failure attribution capability**: n/a — this is a data-improvement / instruction-tuning method, not a failure-attribution or error-localization system; it does not classify failure modes, attribute a responsible agent, or localize a failing step.

- **failure mode addressed**:

> Targets low-quality and student-INCOMPATIBLE instruction-tuning data: noisy, overly simple, or misaligned instruction-response pairs, and (its distinctive contribution) teacher-'improved' rewrites that are not actually beneficial to the specific student model. Loosely maps to 'superficial / low-quality supervision' and teacher-student distribution mismatch rather than any specific MAST multi-agent failure mode; addresses weak instruction difficulty (via IFD) and poor instruction-response feasibility/matching (via r-IFD).

- **dataset or benchmark released**:

> Yes — selectively-recycled datasets (sRecycled Alpaca, sRecycled WizardLM) and trained sRecycled models plus code released at https://github.com/tianyi-lab/Reflection_Tuning. The reversed-IFD (r-IFD) metric is introduced as a reusable evaluation/selection schema. No brand-new evaluation benchmark is introduced (uses existing AlpacaEval / Open LLM Leaderboard / MT-Bench).


### Relations

- **builds on**:

> Reflection-Tuning (Li et al., NeurIPS 2023 Workshop / arXiv:2310.11716) — its direct predecessor (teacher-only data recycling). Cherry LLM / IFD score (Li et al., 2023c, arXiv:2308.12032) and Superfiltering (Li et al., 2024b, arXiv:2402.00530) for the IFD metric; Humpback / instruction backtranslation (Li et al., 2023d) motivates r-IFD. Base datasets Alpaca (Taori et al., 2023) and WizardLM/Evol-Instruct (Xu et al., 2023). Related data-quality lines: AlpaGasus (Chen et al., 2023a), DEITA (Liu et al., 2023b), LIFT (Xu et al., 2023b), SelFee (Ye et al., 2023), Orca (Mitra et al., 2023), Self-Instruct (Wang et al., 2023), LIMA (Zhou et al., 2023), 'LLMs can self-improve' (Huang et al., 2023), Constitutional AI / RLAIF (Bai et al., 2022b; Lee et al., 2023), Chain-of-Thought / Tree-of-Thoughts (Wei et al.; Yao et al.), LLM-as-a-judge / MT-Bench (Zheng et al., 2023).

- **extended by or inspired**:

> Cited and extended within the instruction-tuning data-selection / IFD literature: IterSelectTune (arXiv:2410.13464, iterative IFD-based selection), T-SHIRT (Token-Selective Hierarchical Data Selection, arXiv:2506.01317, introduces token-level Selective-IFD), SelectIT (arXiv:2402.16705, uncertainty-aware self-reflection selection), RAISE (Reinforced Adaptive Instruction Selection, EMNLP 2025 Findings), and BIDS / influence-based balanced selection (EMNLP 2025 Findings). More broadly cited in LLM data-synthesis, weak-to-strong filtering, and self-alignment work.

- **citation count**: 85 (Semantic Scholar, paperId ee85c7c666135f4aae32336968f09584029b6a35, as of June 2026); 58 references. Venue confirmed as ACL 2024 Findings (DBLP conf/acl/LiCCHGZ24).


### Other / reserved fields

- **reasoning model native**:

> no — predates and does not target o1/R1-style reasoning models with built-in reflection. Reflection is engineered externally via a teacher LLM over training data, distilled into Llama2-7B/13B (and Vicuna 7B v1.5) student models.

- **on policy distillation link**:

> Closer to student-aware (partially on-policy-flavored) distillation than its predecessor: a teacher reflects/rewrites data (off-policy teacher generation), but the student then selects which rewrites to keep using its OWN IFD/r-IFD statistics computed from the raw base student model, aligning the retained data with the student's distribution before SFT. This 'teacher-student collaboration' / student-compatibility selection foreshadows on-policy-distillation and skill-compatibility ideas, though the final training is still SFT on teacher-generated targets, not true online on-policy distillation.

- **sample efficiency**:

> Very high: near-peak benchmark performance with as few as 926 selectively-recycled WizardLM samples (2% of the 46,325; 57.80 Open LLM avg and 74.29% AlpacaEval), beating LIMA's 1,000 hand-curated samples; full sRecycled sets (37,114 Alpaca / 46,325 WizardLM-7B) are smaller than the base sets yet outperform them and much larger models (13B/65B). Cost per sample = two teacher API passes plus cheap student IFD/r-IFD forward passes; statistics must be recomputed per student model.

<a id="r028-agent-r-training-language-model-agents-to-reflect-via-iterative-self-training"></a>
## Agent-R: Training Language Model Agents to Reflect via Iterative Self-Training

**ID:** R028  **Category:** E (Parametric / learned reflection (training-based))  **Authors:** Siyu Yuan et al.  **Venue:** arXiv preprint (2025)  **Learning locus:** gradient_weight_update  **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.11425

### Basic info

- **name**: Agent-R: Training Language Model Agents to Reflect via Iterative Self-Training

- **year**: 2025

- **authors**: Siyu Yuan, Zehui Chen, Zhiheng Xi, Junjie Ye, Zhengyin Du, Jiecao Chen (Fudan University + ByteDance Seed; equal contribution Siyu Yuan & Zehui Chen)

- **venue**: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2501.11425, cs.AI; v1 submitted 20 Jan 2025, last revised 24 Mar 2025; not yet a peer-reviewed venue at time of writing)

- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.11425

- **code url**: https://github.com/bytedance/Agent-R (also mirrored at https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/Agent-R)


### Core mechanism

- **reflection type**:

> learned-critic-model / search-guided: Agent-R trains the actor model itself to reflect and self-correct (revise) on the fly. Reflection-supervision data is generated via Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS), and the actor model also acts as a model-guided critic that identifies the first erroneous step in a failed trajectory. The reflective ability is then baked into model weights via SFT (rather than verbal in-context critique a la Reflexion).

- **feedback source**:

> environment-reward (final reward r(tau) in [0,1] from the interactive environment determines good vs bad trajectories) combined with model-guided self-critique (the actor model identifies the first error step within its current capability). No human or expert/stronger-model supervision is used; the framework relies entirely on self-play. A small set of ten hand-designed revision-thought templates (rs) seeds the revision-signal text.

- **iteration structure**:

> tree/MCTS-search for data construction (k=8 rollouts per Monte Carlo estimation, max depth d=20) combined with iterative self-training: at each iteration the current actor model re-collects model-guided revision trajectories and is re-fine-tuned via SFT; reported over 3 iterations. Resulting agent performs mid-trajectory revision (episodic-style on-the-fly correction) at inference.

- **reflection object**:

> action trajectory (and the reasoning/revision step inserted into it). Agent-R constructs 'revision trajectories' that splice a failed (bad) trajectory up to the first error step with a correct (good) path sharing the same parent MCTS node, inserting a revision-thought token (rs) at the transition; the model learns to detect an erroneous action mid-trajectory and pivot onto a recovery path. Ultimately the corrective behavior is internalized into model weights via SFT.


### Learning paradigm

- **learning locus**: gradient_weight_update

- **requires training**:

> SFT (iterative supervised fine-tuning over multiple self-training iterations on self-generated revision + good + general trajectories; no PPO/DPO/RL is used by Agent-R itself, though DPO/contrastive baselines such as ETO are compared against).

- **reward or critic model**:

> verifiable reward (environment final reward in [0,1]) used to label good vs bad trajectories, plus self-as-judge: the actor model itself serves as a model-guided critic to locate the first error step within its current capability. No separately trained reward model or external stronger-model critic is used.

- **distillation target**:

> model-weights: the self-reflection / error-recovery capability is distilled into the agent's parameters via iterative SFT on MCTS-constructed revision trajectories (no external memory store, skill library, or prompt artifact is produced).

- **emergent vs engineered**:

> engineered/scaffold-assisted but internalized into weights: reflection is not RL-emergent (no 'aha'-style emergence). It is engineered through an MCTS data-construction pipeline plus ten hand-designed revision-thought templates and a model-guided first-error-step detection mechanism, then trained into the model so the reflective/revision behavior becomes intrinsic at inference.


### Memory mechanism

- **memory type**:

> none (no persistent external memory): Agent-R uses a within-episode interaction context/scratchpad for the agent trajectory; reflection knowledge is stored in model weights rather than in an episodic memory, skill library, or notes store. MCTS search trees are transient data-construction artifacts, not persistent agent memory.

- **memory persistence**:

> within-episode (the agent operates over one multi-turn trajectory at inference with no cross-episode external memory). Learned reflection capability persists in weights cross-task, but there is no explicit experience-memory module.

- **memory curation mechanism**:

> n/a (no external memory to curate). For training-data construction, trajectories are selected via MCTS with reward thresholds that start low (to mitigate the cold-start problem) and are progressively raised across iterations; the good-trajectory mixture weight alpha is gradually increased so good trajectories converge toward optimal, but this is dataset curation, not agent-memory curation.


### Reflection granularity & timing

- **error localization granularity**:

> step-level: the actor model identifies the FIRST erroneous action step within a failed trajectory, and revision/recovery is spliced in starting from that step (transition point t'). Agent-R explicitly contrasts this with a Direct-Revision baseline that only corrects at the terminal step (holistic/outcome-level).

- **intra task vs inter task**:

> intra-task at inference (the agent recovers from errors mid-trajectory within a single task episode), achieved via cross-task / multi-task training: revision trajectories from WebShop, ScienceWorld, and TextCraft are jointly trained (multi-task training found more effective than single-task in Finding 5).

- **failure recovery vs avoidance**:

> mid-trajectory-recovery (correct in-flight): the central contribution is timely on-the-fly revision rather than waiting until the end of a rollout; the agent learns to detect the first error and pivot onto a correct path during the same episode, reducing dead loops.


### Application domain

- **task domains**:

> decision-making / interactive-agent tasks: web-navigation (online shopping), embodied/scientific text-game reasoning, and tool-use/crafting. All are multi-turn interactive environments with partial observation and delayed (terminal) reward.

- **benchmarks**: WebShop, ScienceWorld (SciWorld), and TextCraft, all run on the AgentGym platform. Test sets: 200 tasks (WebShop), 200 (SciWorld), 100 (TextCraft).


### Evaluation results

- **headline result**:

> On Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Agent-R (iterative SFT on MCTS revision trajectories, 3 iterations) reaches an average score of 70.71 across WebShop/SciWorld/TextCraft (WebShop 63.91 reward, SciWorld 70.23 reward, TextCraft 78.00 success rate), versus 65.12 average for the strongest baseline ETO and 20.00 for the untrained Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, i.e. +5.59 points average over baseline methods and +50.71 over the base model.

- **baselines**:

> Closed-source: GPT-3.5-Turbo, GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-4o (gpt-4o-2024-08-06), Claude-3 (Haiku/Sonnet), DeepSeek-Chat. Open-source / trained agents: Llama2-Chat-13B, AgentLM-7B/13B (AgentTuning), Agent-FLAN, base Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B w/ ETO (DPO contrastive), and Llama-3.1-8B w/ Direct-Revision (corrects only at trajectory end). Ablations: w/ Optimal trajectory, w/ Optimal+Good, w/ Optimal+ (GPT-4o-generated optimal).

- **gains vs baseline**:

> Average +5.59 over the strongest comparable baseline ETO (70.71 vs 65.12); +8.35 over Direct-Revision (70.71 vs 62.36); +25.25 over GPT-4o (70.71 vs 45.46); +50.71 over base Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (70.71 vs 20.00). In the revision/self-correction setting (Table 3, continuing failed trajectories), Agent-R reaches average 46.75 at iteration 3 vs 35.67 for Direct-Revision iter 3, 22.63 for GPT-4o, and 13.08 for ETO. Iterative gains for Agent-R: 39.92 (iter1) -> 42.62 (iter2) -> 46.75 (iter3).

- **compute cost profile**:

> Training-heavy data construction: MCTS with k=8 rollouts per Monte Carlo estimation and max depth d=20 per simulation, run over 300 (WebShop)/200 (SciWorld)/200 (TextCraft) sampled tasks, plus 3 iterations of trajectory re-collection and SFT. Per iteration thousands of good and revision trajectories are produced (e.g. WebShop ~9000 good / ~2000 revision data per Table 1). Inference is a single multi-turn rollout (max 100 rounds in main eval, 50 in the revision setting) with no extra reward-model or external-critic calls, so inference cost is comparable to a standard fine-tuned agent rather than a multi-pass verbal-reflection loop. Exact GPU-hours / token counts are not reported in the main text.


### Limitations & critique

- **known limitations**:

> Suffers from a cold-start problem in challenging environments (few optimal trajectories early), mitigated by low initial reward thresholds and mixing good + general (ShareGPT) data; good trajectories introduce noise (r(tau)<=1) and adding only good trajectories to optimal ones can decrease performance. The model-guided first-error detection is bounded by the actor's current capability. Evaluation is limited to three text-based interactive environments with a single 8B backbone (Llama-3.1-8B); no large-scale, multimodal, or real-world web (e.g. WebArena/SWE-bench) evaluation. The method requires environment-provided terminal rewards and many MCTS rollouts (costly). Generalization beyond the trained environments and to other base models is not extensively studied.

- **oracle or external feedback dependency**:

> env-reward: Agent-R depends on the interactive environment's final reward (r(tau) in [0,1]) to distinguish good vs bad trajectories during MCTS data construction. It does NOT use ground-truth step-level labels, human annotation, or a stronger expert model; the per-step error localization is done by the actor model itself (self-verify within current capability). So self-correction is driven by verifiable environment reward rather than oracle labels at test time.

- **self correction efficacy**:

> net-positive: training on Agent-R revision trajectories yields consistent gains over base model, expert-trajectory SFT (AgentLM/Agent-FLAN), contrastive DPO (ETO), and Direct-Revision, and notably reduces dead-loop / repeated-action behavior (Finding 4) while shortening average revision length over iterations (Finding 3). The paper explicitly frames prompt-only intrinsic self-correction as ineffective/degrading and shows that weight-internalized, environment-reward-grounded revision works in interactive settings.

- **calibration effect**:

> not-measured (no explicit calibration/confidence analysis). The closest proxies are loop-avoidance (reduced repeated-action counts) and shorter average revision length, indicating better error detection rather than measured probability calibration.


### Failure analysis

- **failure attribution capability**:

> attributes-failing-step: the actor model identifies the first erroneous action step in a failed trajectory (model-guided transition-point determination), which is a form of step-level failure localization used to construct revision data. It is not a general failure-mode taxonomy classifier or multi-agent responsibility attributor.

- **failure mode addressed**:

> Targets error-loops / dead loops (agents repeating the same action sequence and getting stuck), cascading errors from uncorrected early mistakes, and the inability to recover from errors mid-trajectory (a form of superficial/absent self-reflection in expert-cloned agents). Maps to MAST-style modes such as error-loops and failure to recover; explicitly measures and reduces repeated-action-sequence counts.

- **dataset or benchmark released**:

> No new benchmark released; evaluation uses existing WebShop/ScienceWorld/TextCraft via AgentGym. Code, training scripts, and the MCTS-based revision-trajectory construction pipeline are released at https://github.com/bytedance/Agent-R (so the self-generated revision-trajectory data can be reproduced rather than being distributed as a fixed dataset).


### Relations

- **builds on**:

> MCTS-based agent data generation and tree search for LLMs (e.g. AlphaZero-like/MCTS-for-LLM work); AgentGym interactive-environment platform (Xi et al.); AgentTuning/AgentLM (Zeng et al.) for behavior-cloning expert trajectories and mixing agent + general (ShareGPT) data; ETO (Exploration-based Trajectory Optimization, Song et al.) for contrastive good/bad trajectory training; Direct-Revision (terminal-step correction) baseline; and the broader self-correction literature (e.g. Huang et al. 'LLMs cannot self-correct reasoning yet', Kamoi et al. critical survey, CRITIC, SCoRe) which it positions itself against for interactive multi-turn settings.

- **extended by or inspired**:

> Cited/extended by subsequent agent self-training and step-level credit-assignment work, e.g. STeCa: Step-level Trajectory Calibration for LLM Agent Learning (2025), SPA-RL: Reinforcing LLM Agents via Stepwise Progress Attribution (2025), AgentRM: Enhancing Agent Generalization with Reward Modeling (2025), SAND: Boosting LLM Agents with Self-Taught Action Deliberation (2025), and Skill-SD: Skill-Conditioned Self-Distillation for Multi-turn LLM Agents (2026); also referenced in surveys on self-evolving agents and test-time compute / reasoning economy.

- **citation count**: 56 (Semantic Scholar, as of June 2026; CorpusId 275757809). Google Scholar / NASA ADS list it under arXiv:2501.11425.


### Other / reserved fields

- **reasoning model native**:

> No: Agent-R targets a standard (non-reasoning) instruction-tuned backbone (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) and explicitly trains reflective/revision behavior into it, rather than relying on o1/R1-style models with built-in reflection. It is positioned as an alternative route to reflection for ordinary LLM agents; the paper notes that built-in self-correction is generally ineffective without such training.

- **on policy distillation link**:

> Strongly related: Agent-R is effectively an on-policy self-distillation / self-training loop. Revision trajectories are constructed from the current actor model's own rollouts (the first error step is identified 'within its current capability'), and SFT is performed iteratively on this self-generated data so the agent learns reflection 'based on its current policy' for better learning efficiency. This is closely aligned with on-policy distillation / skill-self-optimization ideas, though Agent-R uses SFT on spliced trajectories rather than KL-style on-policy distillation from a teacher.

- **sample efficiency**:

> Reaches reported gains in 3 self-training iterations; per environment MCTS is run on 300/200/200 sampled tasks with k=8 rollouts and depth 20. Iterative revision-setting scores improve 39.92 -> 42.62 -> 46.75 across iterations 1-3, with the largest jump from base model to iteration 1. The paper frames the model-guided, on-policy construction as yielding 'better learning efficiency' than direct-revision/expert data, but no formal sample-efficiency curve (#trials to a target) is reported.
