<a id="r067-self-challenging-language-model-agents"></a>
## Self-Challenging Language Model Agents

**ID:** R067  **Category:** E (Parametric / learned reflection (training-based))  **Authors:** Zhou et al. (UC Berkeley & FAIR at Meta)  **Venue:** arXiv preprint (2025)  **Learning locus:** gradient_weight_update  **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.01716

### Basic info

- **name**: Self-Challenging Language Model Agents

- **year**: 2025

- **authors**: Yifei Zhou et al. (UC Berkeley & FAIR at Meta); co-authors Sergey Levine, Jason Weston, Xian Li, Sainbayar Sukhbaatar

- **venue**: arXiv preprint

- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.01716


### Core mechanism

- **reflection type**: tool-verified

- **feedback source**: external-tool (code interpreter / Python verification function executing on environment state); reward is the self-generated verification-function outcome (0/1), with no human-annotated ground-truth task set

- **iteration structure**: episodic-retry-with-reset (multi-turn rollouts, max 15 steps per episode, capped) followed by an offline/online RL training loop on self-generated tasks; not tree/MCTS search

- **reflection object**:

> The agent reflects on and modifies its own model weights via RL on self-generated tasks. Distinctively, the 'reflection' loop is two-role self-play: the agent first acts as a challenger that explores the environment and synthesizes verifiable Code-as-Task problems (instruction + verification function + example solution + failure cases), then as an executor trains on them. The artifact modified is model weights; the intermediate artifact generated is a structured, code-verifiable task/skill curriculum.


### Learning paradigm

- **learning locus**: gradient_weight_update

- **requires training**: RL (one-step REINFORCE, equivalent to Rejection Fine-Tuning on successful rollouts in the main results; also explored DPO/preference, online GRPO and PPO) and SFT (in the distillation setting)

- **reward or critic model**:

> verifiable reward — a self-generated Code-as-Task verification function (executable Python) provides a sparse 0/1 outcome reward; no separate trained reward model and no LLM-as-judge for the main self-improvement reward (in contrast to the PAE baseline which uses the same model as judge)

- **distillation target**:

> model-weights — reflection/experience is distilled into the executor policy's weights; the generated reusable artifact is a set of verifiable Code-as-Task problems (a synthetic task curriculum) plus the rollout trajectories used for RL/SFT

- **emergent vs engineered**:

> engineered — the self-challenging challenger/executor self-play and the Code-as-Task structure (instruction + verification function + example solution + 3 failure cases with automatic filtering) are a designed scaffold/framework, not an RL-emergent 'aha' behavior; RL then optimizes weights within this scaffold


### Memory mechanism

- **memory type**: skill-library (a self-generated pool of verifiable Code-as-Task synthetic tasks, ~800 tasks, used as a training curriculum); no persistent episodic scratchpad memory at inference

- **memory persistence**:

> cross-task — the synthesized tasks and the learned weights transfer to out-of-distribution real test tasks within the same environment; the paper notes improvement is mostly environment-specific rather than cross-environment general

- **memory curation mechanism**:

> retrieval-gated / self-curated via automatic filtering: a Code-as-Task is kept only if the example solution passes the verification function AND none of the three failure cases pass; this rejection filtering keeps ~5.2% of full-CaT tasks (vs 47.7% for verification-only, 9.5% for verification+solution), reducing false-negative/false-positive task noise


### Reflection granularity & timing

- **error localization granularity**: holistic/outcome-level — reward is a sparse 0/1 outcome reward from the verification function over the final environment state and answer; no step-level or token-level credit assignment

- **intra task vs inter task**: inter-task — the agent transfers experience by training on a self-generated task curriculum and generalizes to held-out real tasks; it is not within-task refinement of a single answer

- **failure recovery vs avoidance**:

> avoidance-only — improvement comes from RL training that makes the policy succeed more often on subsequent (out-of-distribution) test tasks; there is no explicit mid-trajectory in-flight self-correction mechanism, though in distillation even failed teacher trajectories (containing reflections on mistakes) are used for learning


### Application domain

- **task domains**: tool-use; multi-turn function calling; web-navigation/browsing; customer-service dialogue (decision-making with tool use); code-as-action interface

- **benchmarks**: M3ToolEval (Calculation and Web Browsing environments) and Tau-Bench / TauBench (Retail and Airline environments) — four multi-turn tool-use environments total


### Evaluation results

- **headline result**:

> On Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, an average relative success-rate improvement of 95.8% (over 2x) across four multi-turn tool-use environments using only self-generated training data; self-improvement average Pass@1 rises from 12.0% (base) to 23.5%, and distillation average Pass@1 to 32.2%

- **baselines**:

> Zero-shot Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (base), zero-shot Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, zero-shot GPT-4o (reference), and the prior state-of-the-art Proposer-Agent-Evaluator (PAE) task-synthesis baseline (in both distillation and self-improvement settings)

- **gains vs baseline**:

> Self-improvement setting: SCA reaches average Pass@1 23.5% vs base 12.0% (+11.5 absolute) and vs PAE 12.9% (a +10.6 advantage over PAE Pass@1); PAE degrades or only marginally improves in 3 of 4 partially-observable environments (e.g. Airline Pass@4 drops to 0%). Distillation setting: SCA average Pass@1 32.2% vs base 12.0% (+20 absolute), beating PAE in all 3 partially-observable environments (gain up to +5.2 Pass@1 in Retail). Ablation in M3ToolEval Calculation: offline Rejection-FT/DPO lifts Pass@1 from 20.3% to 31.8%, online GRPO pushes it to 43.2%.

- **compute cost profile**:

> Training-based: generates ~800 synthetic Code-as-Task tasks and ~12k offline rollout trajectories per setting; aggressive filtering means only ~5.2% of full-CaT candidate tasks survive (so many challenger rollouts are discarded). Pass@1 averaged over 4 trials, Pass@4 from same 4 trials. Online RL (GRPO/PPO) gives the best test accuracy but adds infrastructure complexity for on-policy sampling and is unstable (GRPO observed to collapse to 0% if not carefully tuned). Inference cost is a single standard policy at test time (no extra inference multiplier).


### Limitations & critique

- **known limitations**:

> Non-trivial fraction of false-negative tasks remain even after CaT filtering (main failure mode: semantic ambiguity / missing information that is hard to detect), creating a suboptimality gap vs training on oracle tasks; the agent mostly improves environment-specific skills rather than environment-general agentic capability; online RL (GRPO/PPO) is unstable and hyperparameter-sensitive (can collapse to 0%); challenger may hallucinate infeasible/ambiguous tasks; evaluation limited to one base model (Llama-3.1-8B) and four environments.

- **oracle or external feedback dependency**:

> external-tool/verifier — relies on an executable code verifier (self-generated Code-as-Task verification function run by a code interpreter on environment state) rather than human ground-truth labels; it is unsupervised w.r.t. the real task set but the learning signal is grounded in externally-executed verification, not purely intrinsic self-judgment

- **self correction efficacy**:

> net-positive — yields genuine improvement (over 2x average) on held-out real tasks without label leakage because reward comes from executable verification functions; efficacy is task-dependent (larger gains in fully-observable environments; harder/partially-observable environments still improve but are limited by residual false-negative tasks)


### Failure analysis

- **failure attribution capability**: n/a

- **failure mode addressed**:

> Addresses the lack of high-quality, verifiable training tasks for RL agents: targets low-quality/ambiguous/infeasible self-generated tasks and reward-misspecification (false negatives where impossible tasks give reward 0, and false positives where lenient verifiers give reward 1 without fulfilling the instruction); CaT filtering reduces both FN and FP rates relative to the PAE baseline and verification-only/solution-only variants.


### Relations

- **builds on**:

> Proposer-Agent-Evaluator (PAE, Zhou et al. 2024) for autonomous task proposal; Asymmetric Self-Play (Sukhbaatar et al.; OpenAI ASP) for the challenger/executor self-play idea; Self-Instruct (Wang et al.) for self-generated instructions; CodeAct / code-as-action and tool-use agent lines (M3ToolEval, Tau-Bench); RL post-training methods REINFORCE, DPO, PPO, GRPO

- **extended by or inspired**:

> Cited by self-evolving / zero-data agent works including Agent0 (Unleashing Self-Evolving Agents from Zero Data via Tool-Integrated Reasoning), Tool-R0 (Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Tool-Learning from Zero Data), G-Zero (Self-Play for Open-Ended Generation from Zero Data), Multi-Agent Evolve, Scaling Agent Learning via Experience Synthesis, BenchEvolver, MLE-Smith, and Learning to Build the Environment (Self-Evolving Reasoning RL via Verifiable Environment Synthesis)

- **citation count**: 37 (Semantic Scholar, as of mid-2026; CorpusId 279119647)


### Other / reserved fields

- **reasoning model native**:

> no — the method is applied to and validated on a standard instruction-tuned model (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct), not an o1/R1-style native-reflection reasoning model; the reflective self-challenging behavior is supplied by the framework/scaffold rather than emerging from a reasoning model's built-in chain-of-thought

- **on policy distillation link**:

> Strongly related to on-policy/self-distillation: the self-improvement setting uses on-policy executor rollouts with REINFORCE/Rejection-FT and online GRPO/PPO on self-generated tasks; the distillation setting performs SFT on stronger-teacher (Llama-3.1-70B) trajectories over the same self-synthesized task curriculum, i.e. task-curriculum-mediated distillation of skills into a smaller model's weights

- **sample efficiency**:

> ~800 synthetic Code-as-Task tasks and ~12k offline rollout trajectories per setting to reach the reported gains; scaling analysis shows scaling the number of distinct synthetic tasks generalizes better out-of-distribution than scaling trajectories-per-task (e.g. 200 tasks can slightly degrade OOD test Pass@1)

<a id="r068-samule-self-learning-agents-enhanced-by-multi-level-reflection"></a>
## SAMULE: Self-Learning Agents Enhanced by Multi-level Reflection

**ID:** R068  **Category:** E (Parametric / learned reflection (training-based))  **Authors:** Ge et al. (AWS / Amazon)  **Venue:** EMNLP 2025 (Main)  **Learning locus:** hybrid  **URL:** https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.839/

### Basic info

- **name**: SAMULE: Self-Learning Agents Enhanced by Multi-level Reflection

- **year**: 2025

- **authors**: Yubin Ge, Salvatore Romeo, Jason Cai, Monica Sunkara, Yi Zhang (AWS AI Labs / Amazon)

- **venue**: EMNLP 2025 (Main Conference); Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, Suzhou, China, pp. 16591-16610 (DOI 10.18653/v1/2025.emnlp-main.839)

- **paper url**: https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.839/ (arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.20562)


### Core mechanism

- **reflection type**:

> learned-critic-model — a separate retrospective language model (Qwen 2.5 3B) is SFT-trained to generate trajectory-specific reflections; training-data reflections are synthesized via verbal self-critique against reference outputs across three granularities (micro/meso/macro). At inference, the trained retrospective model produces the verbal critique that guides the actor.

- **feedback source**:

> Hybrid. During offline reflection synthesis: ground-truth-oracle/reference (a valid reference plan ytrain) plus environment outcome (success/fail signal from official evaluation scripts / cost-calculation environment) and self-generated diagnoses. At inference, the trained retrospective model is self-contained and needs no reference; in the interactive setting feedback comes from comparing predicted vs. actual user/environment responses (foresight-based reflection).

- **iteration structure**:

> episodic-retry-with-reset — Reflexion-style trials (at most K, with K=4 trials at inference per Appendix A). Each failed trial yields a reflection appended to the next trial's context. In the interactive setting, foresight-based reflection triggers mid-interaction corrections at each turn.

- **reflection object**:

> action trajectory + reasoning chain — the retrospective model reflects on the agent's full ReAct trajectory (thought/action/observation steps) and produces a verbal diagnosis plus a revised high-level plan that is fed back as context (prompt augmentation). The underlying improvement artifact distilled is the reflection-generating model's weights (the retrospective model is SFT-trained), while the actor LLM itself is not weight-updated.


### Learning paradigm

- **learning locus**: hybrid

- **requires training**:

> SFT — the retrospective model (Qwen 2.5 3B) is trained via supervised fine-tuning (LoRA) on multi-level synthesized reflection data. No RL is used (the paper explicitly shows SFT beats the RL-based Retroformer variant). The actor LLM (Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet) is frozen / used only in-context.

- **reward or critic model**:

> separate retrospective model — a dedicated SFT-trained language model that generates reflections (critiques). No trained scalar reward model or RL critic is used; the reference output (oracle) and outcome success serve as the offline supervision signal for synthesizing the reflection targets.

- **distillation target**:

> model-weights — the synthesized multi-level reflections are distilled (via SFT) into the weights of a small retrospective model that generates reflections at inference. Secondarily, an error taxonomy (structured rules/notes) is built offline; but the inference-time learned artifact is the retrospective model's parameters.

- **emergent vs engineered**:

> engineered — reflection is scaffolded via designed prompts and a hand-structured three-level synthesis pipeline (Single-Trajectory / Intra-Task / Inter-Task), with the reflective behavior then distilled into a model via SFT. It is not RL-emergent (no 'aha'-style emergence); it extends the Reflexion prompt-engineered lineage with a trained reflection generator.


### Memory mechanism

- **memory type**:

> structured-notes/graph + long-term-episodic — an offline-constructed error taxonomy (a structured set of categorized error types) plus per-task/per-trajectory episodic reflections stored during synthesis. At inference the 'memory' is effectively parameterized inside the retrospective model; in the Reflexion-style loop, reflections are appended to context (scratchpad-style episodic buffer).

- **memory persistence**:

> cross-task — Inter-Task (macro) learning extracts transferable insights clustered across diverse task queries, and the trained retrospective model generalizes across tasks. Within a Reflexion trial loop, reflections persist cross-episode (across retries of the same task).

- **memory curation mechanism**:

> self-summarized/curated — reflections from the three levels are merged via a final LLM summarization step into a single target reflection per trajectory; the error taxonomy is incrementally built (LLM checks the existing taxonomy and appends/merges new error types). The taxonomy is static after the offline phase (a stated limitation). Reference-based error classification filters which errors are retained.


### Reflection granularity & timing

- **error localization granularity**:

> step-level (and multi-granular) — during Intra-Task (meso) learning the LLM labels each action step in a trajectory with an error type to obtain an 'error path', giving step-level localization. This rolls up to response/outcome-level (micro: whole-trajectory diagnosis vs. reference) and task-cluster-level (macro: errors grouped across tasks).

- **intra task vs inter task**:

> both — explicitly spans intra-task (meso: error taxonomy across multiple trials of the SAME task query) and inter-task (macro: transferable insights from same-typed errors across DIFFERENT tasks), plus micro single-trajectory refinement. This three-level design is the paper's core contribution.

- **failure recovery vs avoidance**:

> both — non-interactive setting is avoidance-style (reflect after a failed trial, retry next episode, Reflexion-style); the interactive setting adds mid-trajectory recovery via foresight-based reflection that compares predicted vs. actual user response at each turn and corrects in-flight.


### Application domain

- **task domains**: decision-making / planning, tool-use, and dialogue — long-horizon agentic planning (travel planning, trip/meeting natural-language planning) and tool-agent-user interaction (retail and airline customer-service agents).

- **benchmarks**:

> TravelPlanner; NATURAL PLAN (Trip Planning and Meeting Planning, excluding Calendar Scheduling); Tau-bench (Retail and Airline domains, both non-interactive and interactive). HotpotQA used in Appendix B for the Retroformer-variant validation.


### Evaluation results

- **headline result**:

> On TravelPlanner (Claude 3.5 Sonnet-v2 actor), SAMULE reaches 20.00% Pass Rate vs. 12.78% for the strongest baseline (Retroformer variant), 9.44% Inter-Task Error Reflection, 5.56% Reflexion, 4.44% ReAct, and 0.00% ExpeL — i.e., +7.22 points over the best baseline and ~3.6x Reflexion. With Claude 3.7 Sonnet, SAMULE reaches 29.44% vs. 21.67% (Retroformer variant).

- **baselines**:

> ReAct; Reflexion; ExpeL; Inter-Task Error Reflection (static error-type reflections, an ablation of SAMULE itself); Retroformer variant (SFT + DPO replacing PPO, a memory-efficient re-implementation of Retroformer); Fewshot (for no-environment settings like NATURAL PLAN).

- **gains vs baseline**:

> TravelPlanner (Claude 3.5 Sonnet-v2): SAMULE 20.00 vs. Retroformer variant 12.78 (+7.22). TravelPlanner (Claude 3.7 Sonnet): 29.44 vs. 21.67 (+7.77). NATURAL PLAN Trip (EM Accuracy): 60.31 vs. ExpeL 53.79 / Inter-Task 51.56 / Reflexion 50.00 (+6.52 over ExpeL). NATURAL PLAN Meeting: 48.50 vs. Retroformer variant 44.00 (+4.50). Tau-bench non-interactive (3 trials): Retail 87.83 vs. Reflexion 82.61 (+5.22), Airline 66.00 vs. 56.00 (+10.0). Tau-bench interactive: Retail 75.97 vs. Reflexion 69.75 (+6.22), Airline 55.32 vs. 48.50 (+6.82). Error reduction rate: SAMULE 0.67/0.73/0.53 vs. Reflexion 0.13/0.42/0.22 on TravelPlanner/NATURAL-PLAN-Trip/Meeting.

- **compute cost profile**:

> Inference-time reflection model is lightweight (Qwen 2.5 3B); the actor runs Reflexion-style with up to 4 trials (so roughly up to 4x single-pass inference for the actor plus one retrospective-model call per failed trial). Retrospective-model training: LoRA + DeepSpeed Stage-3, AdamW, lr 5e-5, 15 epochs, batch size 1, on 8x NVIDIA A100, ~1 hour per run. The paper notes the offline multi-level reflection-synthesis phase (trajectory analysis, taxonomy construction, cross-task clustering) is resource-intensive for large/long-trajectory datasets, but it deliberately avoids costly/unstable RL (SFT-only), making training cheaper than the RL-based Retroformer.


### Limitations & critique

- **known limitations**:

> (1) Static error taxonomy — built offline and fixed at inference, so it can become incomplete/outdated on new tasks or unseen failure patterns, limiting continual/lifelong learning. (2) Computational overhead in the offline multi-level reflection-synthesis phase (trajectory analysis, taxonomy construction, cross-task clustering) for large-scale datasets with long trajectories. (3) Dependence on a reference/valid output during training reflection synthesis, which is unavailable in some benchmarks (TravelPlanner uses the 'sole-setting' to keep trajectories tractable; full test set not used because outcomes can't be reflected on). (4) Over-providing the reference (at both micro and meso levels) actually degrades performance (15.56% vs. 20.00%).

- **oracle or external feedback dependency**:

> oracle-label/ground-truth (during training) + env-reward — reflection synthesis relies on a reference 'valid plan' (ytrain) and on success/fail outcomes from official evaluation scripts and the cost-calculation environment. At inference the retrospective model itself needs no reference, but the method's learning signal is fundamentally oracle/outcome-dependent. The ablation shows references are critical at the micro level (no-reference variant 18.33% vs. 20.00% with micro-only reference), confirming external/oracle feedback dependency.

- **self correction efficacy**:

> net-positive — improves consistently over reflection and non-reflection baselines across TravelPlanner, NATURAL PLAN, and Tau-bench, and over the RL-based Retroformer variant, in low-success/failure-dense regimes. Notably it does so without leaking labels at inference (reference used only offline for synthesis). The paper argues naive self-reflection (Reflexion/ExpeL) is insufficient under high task complexity (ExpeL collapses to 0% on TravelPlanner), whereas failure-centric, reference-grounded, multi-level synthesis yields robust gains.


### Failure analysis

- **failure attribution capability**:

> classifies-failure-mode (taxonomy) + attributes-failing-step — the meso-level Intra-Task stage incrementally constructs an explicit error taxonomy and classifies the error type of each action step (producing an 'error path' with per-step critiques/rationales), and the macro level clusters trajectories by shared error type across tasks.

- **failure mode addressed**:

> Domain-specific planning/agent error types rather than MAST's multi-agent taxonomy. The constructed TravelPlanner taxonomy includes ~26 categories, e.g. Budget Constraint Violation, Accommodation Minimum Stay Violation, Accommodation Capacity/Child/Pet/Smoking/Party Policy Violations, Travel Time Scheduling/Planning Error, Restaurant Selection/Timing Error, Transportation Planning/Cost Error, Location Verification Error, Geographic Data Misinterpretation, Query Requirement Mismatch, Incomplete Day Planning, Inefficient Resource Allocation. Conceptually it targets MAST-style 'superficial self-reflection' / inadequate error analysis by replacing generic reflections with diagnosed, step-level, reference-grounded error feedback.

- **dataset or benchmark released**:

> No new dataset or benchmark released; the work uses existing benchmarks (TravelPlanner, NATURAL PLAN, Tau-bench, HotpotQA). It does synthesize multi-level reflection training data and an error taxonomy, but no public release of these artifacts is documented. [uncertain whether synthesized data is released]


### Relations

- **builds on**:

> Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023; verbal reinforcement / self-reflection loop, base structure); ReAct (Yao et al. 2023; base planning algorithm); Retroformer (Yao et al. 2024b; retrospective model trained with policy-gradient/PPO — SAMULE's closest predecessor, replacing RL with reference-grounded multi-level SFT); ExpeL (Zhao et al. 2024; experiential learning from successful trajectories — critiqued as success-reliant); CTRL (Xie et al. 2025; RL-based critique); contrastive retrospection (Sun et al. 2023); Kolb's experiential learning cycle (educational-psychology motivation).

- **extended by or inspired**:

> As an October-2025 EMNLP paper it is too recent for established successors. A closely related contemporaneous AWS Labs project, CLEAR (Contrastive Learning of Experience via Agentic Reflection; awslabs/CLEAR), trains a Context Augmentation Model via reflection-distilled SFT then RL — same research lineage/group direction. [uncertain — no confirmed citing successors yet given citationCount=8]

- **citation count**: 8 (Semantic Scholar, as of June 2026; CorpusId 281525659, DBLP conf/emnlp/GeRCSZ25)


### Other / reserved fields

- **reasoning model native**:

> no — SAMULE targets standard (non-reasoning-native) instruction-tuned actors (Claude 3.5 Sonnet-v2, Claude 3.7 Sonnet) and adds reflection externally via a separately trained retrospective model. It does not rely on or specifically study o1/R1-style built-in reflection; reflection is scaffolded/distilled rather than native.

- **on policy distillation link**:

> Related but off-policy-leaning. Reflection targets are synthesized using the strong actor (Claude 3.5 Sonnet-v2) and oracle references, then distilled via SFT into a small retrospective model (Qwen 2.5 3B) — a form of skill/critique distillation. It is not on-policy distillation in the strict RL sense (no online policy rollouts updating the actor; the actor stays frozen and only its context is improved). The RL baseline (Retroformer variant, SFT+DPO/PPO) is the closer on-policy analogue, which SAMULE deliberately replaces with SFT.

- **sample efficiency**:

> Training run is highly efficient: ~1 hour on 8x A100 (LoRA, 15 epochs) for the 3B retrospective model, with SFT-only (no rollout-heavy RL). Data is synthesized from up to K=4 retry trials per training task. At inference, up to 4 trials per task. The paper frames SFT-on-good-reflections as more sample/compute-efficient and more stable than RL, but does not report a formal trials-to-target sample-efficiency curve beyond per-trial performance plots (Figure 2).

# F. Reasoning-model self-reflection (o1/R1-era) & its analysis

<a id="r030-deepseek-r1-incentivizes-reasoning-in-llms-through-reinforcement-learning"></a>
## DeepSeek-R1 incentivizes reasoning in LLMs through reinforcement learning

**ID:** R030  **Category:** F (Reasoning-model self-reflection (o1/R1-era) & its analysis)  **Authors:** Guo, Yang, Zhang et al. (DeepSeek-AI)  **Venue:** Nature 2025  **Learning locus:** gradient_weight_update  **URL:** https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09422-z

### Basic info

- **name**: DeepSeek-R1 incentivizes reasoning in LLMs through reinforcement learning

- **year**: 2025

- **authors**:

> DeepSeek-AI (corresponding: research@deepseek.com); Daya Guo, Dejian Yang, Haowei Zhang, Junxiao Song, Ruoyu Zhang, Runxin Xu, Qihao Zhu, Shirong Ma, Peiyi Wang, Xiao Bi, et al. (very large author list, ~200 authors). Lead affiliation: DeepSeek-AI (Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co., affiliated with High-Flyer), China.

- **venue**: Nature 2025 (vol. 645, pp. 633-638; published online 17 Sep 2025; DOI 10.1038/s41586-025-09422-z). Originally arXiv preprint 2501.12948 (22 Jan 2025). Semantic Scholar CorpusID:275789950; PubMed 40962978; PMC12443585.

- **paper url**: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09422-z (arXiv abstract: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.12948)

- **code url**:

> https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1 (trained weights of DeepSeek-R1-Zero, DeepSeek-R1 and six distilled dense models released under MIT license; DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15753193; inference script at https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15753347; models also on HuggingFace).


### Core mechanism

- **reflection type**:

> RL-emergent verbal-self-critique within a single long chain-of-thought, plus an outcome/tool-verified training signal. There is NO learned critic model, NO multi-agent debate, and NO external search/MCTS at inference. The reflective behaviour (revisiting/reevaluating prior steps, self-verification, exploring alternative approaches, the 'aha moment') emerges spontaneously inside the model's own CoT as a by-product of GRPO RL against verifiable rewards. The improvement SIGNAL is verifiable reward (rule-based accuracy + format), i.e. tool/oracle-verified outcomes, distilled into weights; the reflective COMPETENCE is emergent in-context self-critique. Best summarized as: RL-emergent in-CoT self-reflection/verification trained via verifiable-reward RL.

- **feedback source**:

> environment-reward / verifiable-reward, specifically a rule-based reward system: (1) accuracy rewards from ground-truth answer checking (deterministic math answers boxed and string/rule-matched; code competition answers verified by a compiler against predefined test cases) and (2) format rewards enforcing <think>...</think> tags. For DeepSeek-R1's later stages a generative/model-based reward (DeepSeek-V3 as judge for non-rule-checkable data) and trained helpfulness/safety reward models are added. The authors deliberately AVOID outcome/process neural reward models during R1-Zero RL because they invite reward hacking. No human-annotated CoT, no unit-test scaffold beyond the compiler check, no hidden-state probe.

- **iteration structure**:

> For learning: an online RL loop (GRPO) with grouped rollouts per question (16 samples/question, batch 512, reference model refreshed every 400 steps). DeepSeek-R1 adds a multi-stage outer loop: cold-start SFT -> reasoning-oriented RL -> rejection-sampling SFT (~800k samples) -> preference/alignment RL. At INFERENCE the model is single-pass (one long CoT) but performs iterative-refine-like behaviour WITHIN that single chain (it revisits and reevaluates steps); optional majority-voting/self-consistency (cons@64 / cons@16) is reported as an add-on. It is NOT episodic-retry-with-reset, NOT tree/MCTS search (MCTS was tried and abandoned), NOT population/evolutionary.

- **reflection object**:

> Primarily model weights (the policy is updated by RL so that it natively produces self-reflective reasoning chains). The unit being reflected on/modified at inference is the reasoning chain (CoT): the model revisits and reevaluates its own intermediate reasoning steps, verifies partial results, and switches strategy mid-chain. It does NOT modify prompts/context, maintain an episodic memory store, edit a skill library, or alter its own code; the reusable artifact produced (for distillation) is the set of reasoning trajectories, but the locus of change for the method itself is weights + the emergent in-CoT reasoning trace.


### Learning paradigm

- **learning locus**:

> gradient_weight_update. The core contribution is realized through large-scale RL (GRPO) gradient updates on DeepSeek-V3-Base; reasoning/self-reflection capability is baked into parameters. (At inference the model then exhibits in-context verbal self-reflection, but that capability is a product of the weight update, not an in-context-only scaffold.) Distillation to smaller models is via SFT (also weight updates).

- **requires training**:

> RL (GRPO / online, group-relative policy optimization) is the central method. DeepSeek-R1-Zero = pure RL on the base model with NO SFT cold start. DeepSeek-R1 = nested-RL+SFT: cold-start SFT (thousands of long-CoT examples) -> reasoning RL (GRPO) -> rejection-sampling SFT on ~800k samples (600k reasoning + 200k non-reasoning, 2 epochs) -> a second preference/alignment RL stage (rule-based reasoning rewards + helpfulness/safety reward models). Distilled models (1.5B-70B) use SFT only (no RL).

- **reward or critic model**:

> verifiable reward (rule-based: accuracy + format) is the primary signal and the headline claim (pure verifiable-reward RL incentivizes reasoning). GRPO uses NO value/critic network (advantages are estimated from the group reward distribution instead of a learned baseline). The authors explicitly REJECT neural process reward models (PRM) and outcome reward models for the main RL because of reward hacking. Later R1 stages add a generative reward (DeepSeek-V3-as-judge) for non-verifiable data and trained helpfulness (pairwise, 66k pairs) and safety (pointwise, 106k prompts) reward models for alignment.

- **distillation target**:

> model-weights (twofold). (1) The RL-discovered self-reflective reasoning is distilled into the policy's own weights. (2) Explicitly, the reasoning patterns of the large DeepSeek-R1 are distilled into six smaller dense models (Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B/7B, Qwen2.5-14B/32B, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct) by SFT on ~800k DeepSeek-R1-generated reasoning samples. The paper shows distillation from the large model BEATS running RL directly on the small model (e.g., on Qwen2.5-32B), establishing model-weight distillation as a key deliverable. Not episodic-memory, skill-library, prompt, or constitution.

- **emergent vs engineered**:

> RL-emergent (this is the canonical example). DeepSeek-R1-Zero is explicitly the first open demonstration that self-reflection, verification and dynamic strategy adaptation EMERGE from pure RL against verifiable rewards, without any prompt/scaffold engineering of the reflection itself and without human CoT demonstrations. Hallmarks: spontaneously increasing 'thinking time'/response length over training; the 'aha moment' (a sudden spike in the word 'wait' and self-reevaluation in an intermediate checkpoint). Contrast with Reflexion/Self-Refine, where reflection is prompt/scaffold-engineered. (The DeepSeek-R1 production pipeline does add engineered stages -- cold-start SFT, rejection sampling, alignment RL -- but the reasoning behaviour itself is RL-emergent.)


### Memory mechanism

- **memory type**:

> short-term/scratchpad. The only 'memory' is the within-response chain-of-thought (the <think>...</think> reasoning trace / extended thinking tokens), which functions as a scratchpad the model writes and re-reads/revises during a single generation. There is NO external long-term episodic memory, skill library, structured note graph, or cross-session playbook. Persistence of learned skill is at the parameter level (weights), not an external memory store.

- **memory persistence**:

> within-episode for the scratchpad/CoT (it does not carry over between separate queries). The learned reasoning ability is persisted in weights and is therefore cross-task / cross-session at the capability level (it generalizes across all reasoning problems and is available in every deployment). No retained per-episode experience buffer across inference calls.

- **memory curation mechanism**:

> n/a for an explicit memory module (there is no external memory to curate). The closest analogue is data curation in the R1 pipeline: rejection sampling from the RL checkpoint retains only correct trajectories, filters out CoT with language mixing / overly long paragraphs / code blocks, and assembles ~800k SFT samples; a generative reward model (DeepSeek-V3) judges non-rule-checkable cases. Within a single CoT, 'curation' is the model's own emergent self-verification/re-evaluation (overwrite-by-rethinking), not a stored-memory management policy.


### Reflection granularity & timing

- **error localization granularity**:

> Training signal is holistic/outcome-level: the reward is computed on the FINAL answer correctness (+ a format check on the whole response); there is deliberately NO step-level / process-level credit assignment (the authors abandoned process reward models / PRM). However, the EMERGENT in-CoT self-reflection operates at step-level/block-level: within its reasoning chain the model revisits, reevaluates and corrects individual prior steps. So: outcome-level reward driving emergent step-level self-correction.

- **intra task vs inter task**:

> Both, at different layers. The trained capability is inter-task: RL produces a reasoner whose self-reflective skill transfers across all reasoning problems and to held-out benchmarks (and is distillable to other models). At inference, the self-correction is intra-task: within a single problem's long CoT the model refines its own reasoning before answering. It does NOT transfer episodic experience across separate task instances at test time (no cross-episode memory like Reflexion/ExpeL).

- **failure recovery vs avoidance**:

> mid-trajectory-recovery (emergent). Within a single reasoning chain the model corrects course in-flight: it reevaluates its initial approach, allocates more thinking time, and explores alternative solution paths before committing to a final answer (the 'aha moment' is exactly this in-flight reconsideration). It is not avoidance-by-retry-next-episode (no reset/retry loop) and not post-hoc revision of an already-emitted answer.


### Application domain

- **task domains**:

> Primarily verifiable reasoning: math, code (competitive programming), and QA/reasoning + STEM/science (graduate-level physics/chemistry/biology). Also general-alignment (helpfulness/harmlessness) and writing/open-domain QA via the later R1 stages. Reported weaker on agentic/engineering: software engineering, function calling, multi-turn, complex role-playing, structured JSON output.

- **benchmarks**:

> AIME 2024 (pass@1 and cons@64 / cons@16), MATH-500, CNMO 2024, GPQA Diamond, Codeforces (Elo rating + percentile), LiveCodeBench (2024-08 to 2025-01), SWE-bench Verified, Aider, MMLU / MMLU-Redux / MMLU-Pro, C-Eval, CMMLU, DROP, IFEval, FRAMES, SimpleQA / C-SimpleQA, AlpacaEval 2.0, Arena-Hard, HumanEval-Mul. Distilled models reported on AIME 2024, MATH-500, GPQA Diamond, Codeforces, LiveCodeBench.


### Evaluation results

- **headline result**:

> Pure RL (DeepSeek-R1-Zero, GRPO on DeepSeek-V3-Base, no SFT) raises AIME 2024 pass@1 from 15.6% to 71.0% (Nature revised value 77.9%), and to 86.7% with self-consistency/majority voting, matching/surpassing OpenAI-o1-0912. DeepSeek-R1 (full multi-stage pipeline) reaches AIME 2024 79.8% pass@1, MATH-500 97.3%, GPQA Diamond 71.5%, Codeforces 2,029 Elo (96.3rd percentile, ~expert level), comparable to OpenAI-o1-1217.

- **baselines**:

> OpenAI-o1-1217 and OpenAI-o1-mini and OpenAI-o1-0912 (frontier reasoning models), DeepSeek-V3 (its own non-reasoning base via conventional post-training), Claude-3.5-Sonnet-1022, GPT-4o-0513. For distilled models: QwQ-32B-Preview and the base Qwen2.5 / Llama3 instruct models, and RL-on-small-model (Qwen2.5-32B-RL) as an internal comparison.

- **gains vs baseline**:

> DeepSeek-R1-Zero AIME 2024: +55.4 absolute (15.6% -> 71.0% pass@1; Nature: -> 77.9%), reaching o1-0912 level from a base near random. DeepSeek-R1 vs DeepSeek-V3 (its conventionally-trained sibling, same V3-Base): AIME 2024 79.8% vs 39.2%, MATH-500 97.3% vs 90.2%, GPQA Diamond 71.5% vs 59.1%, Codeforces 2029 vs 1134 Elo, LiveCodeBench 65.9% vs 36.2% -- large RL-driven gains. vs OpenAI-o1-1217: R1 slightly surpasses on AIME 2024 (79.8 vs 79.2) and is on par on MATH-500 (97.3 vs 96.4); slightly below o1 on some knowledge benchmarks. Distillation: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B (72.6 AIME, 94.3 MATH-500, 62.1 GPQA, 57.2 LiveCodeBench) far exceeds QwQ-32B-Preview (50.0 AIME) and beats running RL directly on Qwen2.5-32B; Distill-Qwen-7B (55.5 AIME) beats GPT-4o-0513 (9.3) and QwQ-32B-Preview.

- **compute cost profile**:

> Training: large-scale RL (described as costly; precise FLOPs/$ in Supplementary Information 2.4.4, not in the main text). RL hyperparameters (R1 first stage): lr 3e-6, KL coeff 0.001, GRPO clip eps 10, sampling temp 1, 16 rollouts/question, max length 32,768 tokens, 32 questions/step (batch 512), reference model refreshed every 400 steps; 8,192 rollouts per generation split into 16 minibatches, single inner epoch. GRPO is cheaper than PPO (no value network ~ halves the trainable model footprint). Inference: a reasoning model -> markedly higher token cost than single-pass (hundreds-to-thousands of CoT tokens, capped at 32,768), but dynamically allocated by problem difficulty (fewer tokens for easy, more for hard). Distillation amortizes inference cost into much smaller dense models. Overthinking on easy questions is noted as residual inefficiency.


### Limitations & critique

- **known limitations**:

> (1) DeepSeek-R1-Zero suffers poor readability and language mixing (English/Chinese mixed in one CoT) -- the motivation for the R1 cold-start pipeline. (2) Prompt sensitivity: few-shot prompting consistently DEGRADES R1; authors recommend zero-shot, direct problem statement. (3) General capability gaps vs DeepSeek-V3 in function calling, multi-turn, complex role-playing, and JSON output. (4) Language mixing persists for non-Chinese/English queries. (5) Software-engineering tasks under-improved because long eval times limited RL there (SWE-bench Verified ~ comparable to V3, not dominant). (6) Overthinking: excessive reasoning on simple questions; token-efficiency room remains. (7) Reward hacking risk: pure RL needs reliable verifiable rewards; for non-verifiable tasks (e.g. writing) reliable rewards are hard, so R1 falls back to SFT + only a few hundred RL steps. (8) Unsuccessful attempts documented: PRM (hard to define fine-grained steps, hard to judge step correctness, reward hacking) and MCTS (token search space explosion, value-model training hard) both failed to scale. (9) Safety: jailbreakable; inherent safety only 'moderate' (~GPT-4o-2024-05-13) without an external risk-control system; refuses some queries after safety RL (hurts C-SimpleQA).

- **oracle or external feedback dependency**:

> env-reward / verifiable-reward (effectively oracle-label for the training signal). The method fundamentally depends on a RELIABLE VERIFIER: ground-truth answers for math (rule/string match) and a compiler + test cases for code. The authors state the key to unlocking reasoning is 'hard reasoning questions, a reliable verifier and sufficient compute.' This is the discriminating variable: R1's self-reflection is incentivized via objective external/automated verification during training, not via intrinsic-only self-verification. At inference it self-verifies intrinsically (no external tool), but that ability was bought with verifiable-reward RL. Where no reliable verifier exists (writing, open-ended), the approach degrades to SFT/limited RL.

- **self correction efficacy**:

> net-positive but requires-(verifiable)-reward. With a reliable verifier, RL reliably and dramatically improves reasoning and the emergent self-verification/reflection genuinely raises accuracy on held-out reasoning benchmarks (distinct from the Huang-2023/'cannot self-correct yet' intrinsic-only negative result -- here the corrective skill is RL-trained against an oracle, not free intrinsic self-correction). Efficacy is contingent on a trustworthy reward signal; for tasks lacking one (writing), pure-RL self-improvement does not scale. So: strongly net-positive on verifiable reasoning, task-dependent / requires-oracle otherwise.

- **calibration effect**:

> mixed / largely not-measured as formal confidence calibration. The model exhibits productive 'reasoning tax' trade-offs: a language-consistency reward slightly degrades accuracy but improves readability; safety RL causes some over-refusal (lower C-SimpleQA). Overthinking on easy questions is documented (a soft over-allocation/overconfidence-in-need-to-reason effect). The paper does not report explicit ECE/Brier-style calibration metrics for answer confidence, so formal calibration is not-measured; behaviourally the effect is mixed (gains on hard problems, occasional overthinking/over-refusal).


### Failure analysis

- **failure attribution capability**:

> n/a. DeepSeek-R1 is a reasoning-model training method, not a failure-attribution/diagnosis system; it does not classify failure modes into a taxonomy, attribute a responsible agent, or perform counterfactual step localization. (It uses only outcome-level verifiable rewards and documents its own 'unsuccessful attempts' qualitatively, but performs no algorithmic failure attribution.)

- **failure mode addressed**:

> Targets the data-bottleneck and human-bias-ceiling of reasoning training (dependence on human-annotated CoT that caps performance at human-like reasoning) by letting RL discover non-human reasoning strategies. The emergent behaviours directly mitigate MAST-style failure modes: superficial/absent self-reflection (-> emergent reflection & self-verification), underthinking / premature termination on hard problems (-> learns to allocate more thinking time and explore alternatives). Conversely it can INDUCE overthinking (excess reasoning on easy items) and is exposed to reward hacking when the verifier is unreliable. R1-Zero's own failure modes (language mixing, poor readability) motivate the multi-stage R1.

- **dataset or benchmark released**:

> No new failure-trace benchmark. Released: model weights for DeepSeek-R1-Zero, DeepSeek-R1, and six distilled dense models (1.5B/7B/8B/14B/32B/70B) under MIT license; sample data used in rejection sampling and RL prompts; inference scripts. (Zenodo DOIs 10.5281/zenodo.15753193 and 10.5281/zenodo.15753347.) These open-weights/open-data releases are themselves the major reusable resource that seeded a large open RL-reasoning ecosystem.


### Relations

- **builds on**:

> GRPO (Shao et al., 2024, DeepSeekMath) as the RL algorithm; PPO (Schulman et al., 2017) as the predecessor it simplifies; DeepSeek-V3 / DeepSeek-V3-Base (DeepSeek-AI, 2024) as the base model; chain-of-thought prompting (Wei et al., 2022) and 'let's think step by step' (Kojima et al., 2022); self-consistency / majority voting (Wang et al., 2022); OpenAI o1 (2024) as the inference-time-scaling reasoning-model paradigm it open-replicates; the RL-from-verifiable-reward / RLHF lineage (Ouyang et al. 2022). Implicitly part of the STaR / RL'd self-improvement-of-reasoning lineage (Zelikman et al. 2022; expert iteration). Explicitly contrasts with process reward models (Uesato 2022; Lightman 2023) and MCTS (AlphaGo/AlphaZero, Silver 2017) which it tried and abandoned.

- **extended by or inspired**:

> Catalyzed the 2025 'RL with verifiable rewards' (RLVR) and open-reasoning wave: open replications/analyses of R1-Zero such as Open-R1 (Hugging Face), TinyZero, SimpleRL-Zoo / SimpleRL-Reason, Logic-RL, Open-Reasoner-Zero, DAPO and Dr.GRPO (GRPO bias fixes); s1 / s1.1 budget-forcing and LIMO ('less is more' for reasoning); analyses of whether RL elicits vs. teaches reasoning (e.g. 'Does RLVR incentivize reasoning beyond the base model?', 'Spurious rewards' studies); reasoning distillation work (e.g. Sky-T1, Bespoke-Stratos, OpenThoughts). Directly informed DeepSeek-R1-0528 and subsequent reasoning models (Qwen3, Kimi k1.5/k2, etc.). Widely treated as the reference open reasoning model for studying emergent self-reflection.

- **citation count**:

> ~5,381 (Semantic Scholar, Nature version, paperId 2eed1fad9bbf887d4395de40f20144c4fafefd7f / CorpusID:275789950, as of June 2026). The arXiv preprint 2501.12948 is among the most-cited AI papers of 2025; combined preprint+journal citations are substantially higher (well into the thousands and rapidly growing).


### Other / reserved fields

- **reasoning model native**:

> yes -- this IS a reasoning model and a defining instance of the o1/R1 era. DeepSeek-R1/-R1-Zero have built-in, always-on, RL-induced long-CoT reasoning with native (RL-emergent) self-reflection, verification and dynamic strategy adaptation; it is the open-weights archetype of a reasoning-model-native system with intrinsic reflection.

- **on policy distillation link**:

> strong / foundational on two axes. (1) RL itself is on-policy improvement: GRPO samples on-policy groups and updates the policy toward higher-reward (verified) trajectories -- self-distillation toward its own best reasoning. (2) Explicit knowledge distillation: ~800k on-policy DeepSeek-R1 trajectories are used to SFT smaller models, and the paper empirically shows distilling the large model's reasoning beats running RL on the small model. This positions R1 as a key reference for the on-policy-distillation / RLVR vs. distillation debate (teacher-trajectory SFT vs. small-model RL).

- **sample efficiency**:

> RL: gains accrue over thousands of RL steps (AIME 15.6%->71% across the training trajectory shown in Fig.1/2), with 16 rollouts/question and batch 512; substantial but not enormous step count by RL standards (reference model refreshed every 400 steps). Cold-start needs only 'thousands' of long-CoT examples; rejection-sampling SFT uses ~800k samples (600k reasoning + 200k non-reasoning, 2 epochs). The headline efficiency claim is data efficiency vs human annotation: no human-annotated reasoning traces are required for the core capability (only a verifier + hard questions). Distillation is highly sample/compute efficient at deployment (capability transferred to 1.5B-70B via SFT).

<a id="r031-s1-simple-test-time-scaling"></a>
## s1: Simple test-time scaling

**ID:** R031  **Category:** F (Reasoning-model self-reflection (o1/R1-era) & its analysis)  **Authors:** Muennighoff, Yang, Shi et al.  **Venue:** EMNLP 2025  **Learning locus:** hybrid  **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19393

### Basic info

- **name**: s1: Simple test-time scaling

- **year**: 2025

- **authors**: Niklas Muennighoff, Zitong Yang, Weijia Shi, Xiang Lisa Li et al. (Stanford University; co-authored with University of Washington, Allen Institute for AI, Contextual AI)

- **venue**: EMNLP 2025 (Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, pp. 20275-20321); originally arXiv:2501.19393, Jan 2025

- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19393 (ACL Anthology: https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.1025/)

- **code url**: https://github.com/simplescaling/s1 (model, data s1K, and code open-source; s1-32B weights and s1K-1.1 dataset released)


### Core mechanism

- **reflection type**:

> verbal-self-critique elicited via decoding-time intervention: 'budget forcing' suppresses the end-of-thinking token and appends 'Wait' to force the model to continue thinking, which leads it to double-check and self-correct its in-progress reasoning; not a learned critic and not tool-verified.

- **feedback source**:

> self-generated. There is no external verifier, unit test, oracle label, or environment reward at inference time; the extra 'Wait'-induced thinking is the model re-examining its own reasoning. (Training signal is SFT on Gemini-distilled reasoning traces, also not verifier-gated.)

- **iteration structure**:

> iterative-refine via sequential test-time scaling: the model generates a single long reasoning trace whose length is controlled by budget forcing; appending 'Wait' 2/4/6 times forces additional self-correction rounds within one trajectory (the authors classify this as sequential, not parallel, scaling, contrasting it with majority voting).

- **reflection object**:

> reasoning chain (the in-progress chain-of-thought / 'thinking' segment): budget forcing forces the model to keep extending and revising its current reasoning trace, often fixing incorrect intermediate steps before committing to a final answer. Secondarily the method modifies model weights once via SFT on 1,000 reasoning traces, but the test-time self-correction operates on the reasoning chain itself.


### Learning paradigm

- **learning locus**: hybrid

- **requires training**:

> SFT (supervised fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct on the 1,000-example s1K reasoning-trace dataset; ~26 minutes on 16 H100 GPUs). The self-correction/test-time-scaling behavior at inference is in-context (no weight update); budget forcing is a decoding-time intervention requiring no further training.

- **reward or critic model**:

> none. No reward model or trained critic is used. Reasoning traces for SFT are distilled from Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking Experimental; the model self-corrects at test time without any external judge. Self-as-judge only in the implicit sense that the model re-examines its own reasoning when forced to continue.

- **distillation target**:

> model-weights (reasoning ability distilled from Gemini Thinking traces into Qwen2.5-32B via SFT on s1K). The test-time self-correction itself is not distilled into a reusable artifact; it is elicited live by the budget-forcing decoding rule.

- **emergent vs engineered**:

> scaffold/decoding-engineered. Unlike R1's RL-emergent 'aha'/self-verification, s1's self-correction is hand-engineered: a hard-coded decoding intervention that appends the literal string 'Wait' (and suppresses the end-of-thinking delimiter) to force the model to reconsider. The underlying reasoning capability is hypothesized to be latent from pretraining and merely 'activated' by 1K-example SFT (Superficial Alignment Hypothesis, a la LIMA).


### Memory mechanism

- **memory type**: short-term/scratchpad. The long reasoning trace ('thinking' tokens) within a single problem acts as the scratchpad; there is no persistent episodic memory, skill library, or playbook.

- **memory persistence**: within-episode. Self-correction happens within a single problem's reasoning trace; nothing is carried across problems or sessions (the SFT-encoded knowledge is in weights, not an explicit memory store).

- **memory curation mechanism**:

> n/a. No memory store is maintained or curated. (The closest analogue is data curation of s1K itself: the 59K candidate pool is filtered down to 1,000 via the Quality/Difficulty/Diversity selection algorithm, but this is training-data curation, not run-time memory curation.)


### Reflection granularity & timing

- **error localization granularity**:

> step-level (within the reasoning chain): budget forcing makes the model revisit and revise individual intermediate reasoning steps mid-trace (e.g., it tries to stop after '...is 2.' but the forced 'Wait' makes it re-derive and correct that step). The control/scaling is measured at the trace/token-budget (outcome) level, but the self-correction itself targets reasoning steps.

- **intra task vs inter task**: intra-task. Self-correction and refinement occur within a single problem's reasoning trace via additional test-time compute; there is no transfer of experience across tasks at inference.

- **failure recovery vs avoidance**:

> mid-trajectory-recovery. By forcing the model to keep thinking ('Wait') instead of terminating, s1 lets the model correct errors in-flight within the same reasoning trajectory (the paper shows it 'double-check[s] its answer, often fixing incorrect reasoning steps'), rather than retrying in a fresh episode.


### Application domain

- **task domains**: math (competition math) and QA/reasoning (PhD-level science questions). Specifically reasoning-intensive tasks; no code, web-navigation, embodied, or dialogue domains.

- **benchmarks**: AIME 2024 (AIME24), MATH500, GPQA Diamond (198 PhD-level science questions). Ablations also use these three; data decontaminated against them with 8-gram matching.


### Evaluation results

- **headline result**:

> After SFT on s1K (1,000 examples) + budget forcing, s1-32B exceeds o1-preview on competition math by up to 27% (MATH500 and AIME24). Test-time scaling via budget forcing extrapolates AIME24 from 50% (no intervention) to 57%. Final s1-32B: AIME24 56.7%, MATH500 93.0%, GPQA Diamond 59.6% (vs base Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct 26.7 / 84.0 / 49.0).

- **baselines**:

> Base model Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct (no reasoning SFT); s1 w/o budget forcing (1K SFT only); API reasoning models o1-preview / o1-mini / o1 and Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking; open-weight reasoning models QwQ-32B, DeepSeek-r1 (>=800K examples) and r1-distill (800K); open-data SFT replications Sky-T1 (17K) and Bespoke-32B (17K). Alternative test-time scaling methods: token-conditional control (TCC), step-conditional control (SCC), class-conditional control (CCC), rejection sampling (RS), and parallel majority voting.

- **gains vs baseline**:

> vs base Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct: AIME24 +30.0 pts (26.7 -> 56.7), MATH500 +9.0 pts (84.0 -> 93.0), GPQA +10.6 pts (49.0 -> 59.6). Budget forcing alone adds +6.7 pts on AIME24 over s1 w/o BF (50.0 -> 56.7). s1-32B beats o1-preview (AIME24 44.6, GPQA 73.3, MATH500 85.5) on AIME24 and MATH500 'by up to 27%' but trails o1-preview on GPQA. Matches/exceeds the open-data Sky-T1 (AIME24 43.3) and is competitive with Bespoke-32B (63.3) using only 1K vs 17K examples; data-efficiency is the key gain. Ablation: 'Wait' 1x->2x->4x raises AIME24 53.3->53.3 -> 56.7 region; training on the full 59K pool gives no substantial gain over the 1K selection, and random/longest-only/diversity-only selection is ~-30% on AIME24.

- **compute cost profile**:

> Training: extremely cheap, ~26 minutes of SFT on 16 H100 GPUs on 1,000 examples (no RL, no reward model) -- vs R1's >=800K examples and RL. Inference: budget forcing increases test-time compute by forcing more thinking tokens (e.g., forcing the model not to stop 2/4/6 times); AIME24 best point uses ~7,320 thinking tokens (f(7320)=57%). Sequential scaling is bounded -- it eventually flattens and is capped by the model's context window. Parallel majority voting is also evaluated (2-64 samples).


### Limitations & critique

- **known limitations**:

> Budget forcing has two stated key limitations when scaling further: (1) performance eventually flattens out (does not monotonically reach 100%), and (2) it is constrained by the underlying model's context window. Repeatedly appending 'Wait' yields diminishing/inverse returns past a point. Rejection sampling shows an inverse scaling trend (longer samples are more often wrong). The method is evaluated only on math/science reasoning; gains depend heavily on the latent reasoning ability of the strong Qwen2.5-32B base (Superficial Alignment Hypothesis) and on high-quality distilled traces from Gemini. Evaluation is also sensitive to non-determinism in vLLM runs.

- **oracle or external feedback dependency**:

> intrinsic-only / self-verify. At test time s1 uses NO external verifier, oracle label, environment reward, or tool feedback -- the model self-corrects purely by being forced to keep thinking. This is a notable contrast to oracle-dependent self-correction critiques (Huang et al., Kamoi et al.): s1's gains come without label leakage, but only because the extra forced computation lets a strong model exploit its own latent reasoning, and the effect is modest and saturating.

- **self correction efficacy**:

> net-positive but task-dependent and saturating. Forcing more thinking via 'Wait' improves competition-math/GPQA accuracy without any oracle (e.g., AIME24 50%->57%), and the paper explicitly reports it 'often fix[es] incorrect reasoning steps'. However, gains flatten with more forced 'Wait's and the related rejection-sampling variant shows inverse scaling, so unbounded self-correction is not net-positive.

- **calibration effect**: not-measured. The paper measures task accuracy and controllability/scaling slope of test-time compute, not confidence calibration or a 'reasoning tax'; calibration effects of budget forcing are not reported.


### Failure analysis

- **failure attribution capability**:

> n/a. s1 is a method/model for eliciting test-time scaling and self-correction, not a failure-attribution or failure-classification system; it does not classify failure modes, attribute responsible agents, or localize failing steps as a diagnostic output.

- **failure mode addressed**:

> Targets 'underthinking' / premature termination of reasoning: by suppressing the end-of-thinking token and appending 'Wait', budget forcing prevents the model from stopping too early and induces deeper reasoning and in-flight self-correction. The flip side (saturation and inverse scaling from over-forcing 'Wait') exposes an 'overthinking'-style failure where additional forced reasoning no longer helps or hurts.

- **dataset or benchmark released**:

> Yes -- s1K: 1,000 curated questions paired with reasoning traces and solutions (distilled from Gemini Thinking), plus the underlying 59K-example candidate pool, the s1-32B model weights, and full code. An improved s1.1 model and s1K-1.1 dataset (R1-distilled traces) were also released.


### Relations

- **builds on**:

> OpenAI o1 (test-time scaling, the target being replicated); Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct (base model); Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking Experimental (source of distilled reasoning traces); LIMA / Superficial Alignment Hypothesis (Zhou et al. 2023, motivating 1K-example sufficiency); test-time-compute scaling literature (Snell et al. 2024; Brown et al. 2024 on repeated/parallel sampling); lm-evaluation-harness (Gao et al.). Conceptually parallel to DeepSeek-R1 and Kimi k1.5 (RL-based o1 replications) which it contrasts against.

- **extended by or inspired**:

> Spawned a wave of sample-efficient reasoning-SFT and test-time-scaling work and is a canonical reference/baseline for o1/R1-era reasoning replication and inference-time control. Direct successors include the authors' own s1.1 (R1-distilled traces) and the broader 'budget forcing'/controllable-thinking-budget line of work; frequently cited alongside LIMO ('Less is More for Reasoning') and other 1K-scale reasoning-distillation efforts. (Specific named downstream papers not enumerated in the source; treated as inspiring the controllable-test-time-compute and minimal-SFT-reasoning literature.)

- **citation count**: approx. 1,271 (Semantic Scholar, CorpusID:276079693, as of June 2026); Google Scholar lists ~1,255 for the s1 entry. Reference count 98.


### Other / reserved fields

- **reasoning model native**:

> Yes -- s1 explicitly targets o1/R1-style reasoning models with an explicit 'thinking' phase; it both creates such a model (s1-32B has a thinking segment delimited by an end-of-thinking token) and controls it. Budget forcing presupposes a model that emits a separable thinking trace, so the method is native to reasoning models and would not apply to non-thinking LLMs without that structure.

- **on policy distillation link**:

> Off-policy SFT distillation, not on-policy distillation: s1 distills static reasoning traces from a teacher (Gemini Thinking) into Qwen2.5-32B via standard supervised fine-tuning on a fixed 1K dataset -- the student does not generate its own rollouts that are then graded/relabeled. It is the data-efficiency counterpoint to on-policy distillation / RL approaches (DeepSeek-R1), showing that minimal off-policy SFT plus a decoding-time intervention rivals RL-trained reasoners; relevant to OPD discussions as the 'simple SFT + test-time control' baseline.

- **sample efficiency**:

> Extremely high training sample efficiency: only 1,000 SFT examples (s1K) suffice to make Qwen2.5-32B competitive with o1-preview, vs >=800K examples for r1/r1-distill and 17K for Sky-T1/Bespoke-32B; training on the full 59K pool gives no substantial gain over the 1K selection. Test-time: budget forcing's gain (AIME24 50->57%) comes from a single trace extended with ~2-6 forced 'Wait's; majority voting uses up to 64 samples for the parallel baseline.

<a id="r032-let-lrms-break-free-from-overthinking-via-self-braking-tuning"></a>
## Let LRMs Break Free from Overthinking via Self-Braking Tuning

**ID:** R032  **Category:** F (Reasoning-model self-reflection (o1/R1-era) & its analysis)  **Authors:** Yan et al. (ZJU-REAL)  **Venue:** arXiv 2025  **Learning locus:** gradient_weight_update  **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.14604

### Basic info

- **name**: Let LRMs Break Free from Overthinking via Self-Braking Tuning

- **year**: 2025

- **authors**: Haoran Zhao, Yuchen Yan, Yongliang Shen et al. (lead affiliation: Zhejiang University, ZJU-REAL; with Tianjin University and Microsoft Research Asia)

- **venue**: NeurIPS 2025 (arXiv preprint 2505.14604, submitted May 2025; camera-ready Oct 2025)

- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.14604

- **code url**: https://github.com/ZJU-REAL/Self-Braking-Tuning (project page: https://zju-real.github.io/SBT/)


### Core mechanism

- **reflection type**:

> learned-critic-model (the LRM is trained, via SFT on curated adaptive-length data, to internalize a self-regulating 'braking' behavior that recognizes when reasoning has become redundant and terminates it; reflection is over the model's own chain of thought rather than via an external critic)

- **feedback source**:

> ground-truth-oracle (overthinking is identified offline using the reasoning efficiency ratio measured against standard/correct answers — the position of the first correct answer in the trajectory — plus a curated lexicon of overthinking marker terms; this oracle signal is used only during training-data construction, not at inference)

- **iteration structure**:

> single-shot (at inference the SBT-tuned model produces one reasoning trajectory and autonomously stops; the data-construction pipeline analyzes existing OpenR1-Math trajectories step-by-step offline, but the deployed model is single-pass with no test-time iteration/retry)

- **reflection object**:

> reasoning chain (the chain-of-thought is the object: SBT prunes redundant Evolution Solutions from the reasoning trajectory and inserts metacognitive 'braking'/epiphany sentences); the learning is ultimately written into model weights via SFT, so it also modifies model weights


### Learning paradigm

- **learning locus**: gradient_weight_update (SBT is supervised fine-tuning on the SBT-E / SBT-D adaptive-length datasets, i.e. the self-regulation behavior is baked into model weights; no in-context-only mechanism)

- **requires training**: SFT (supervised fine-tuning on OpenR1-Math-SBT-E and OpenR1-Math-SBT-D, each 92,064 examples, with loss masking on the retained redundant 'braking' segment)

- **reward or critic model**:

> verifiable reward used offline for data labeling (overthinking is detected with a verifiable, standard-answer-based reasoning efficiency ratio plus an overthink-marker lexicon, combined into an overthink score with weight beta=0.1); no online reward model or RL critic is used during training

- **distillation target**:

> model-weights (the self-braking behavior is distilled into the LRM's weights via SFT); the intermediate reusable artifacts are the two released training datasets OpenR1-Math-SBT-E and OpenR1-Math-SBT-D, each ~92K adaptive-length trajectories

- **emergent vs engineered**:

> engineered training-data signal that induces emergent inference behavior: the truncation rule, overthink metrics, masking, and natural-language braking prompts are engineered, but after SFT the model spontaneously generates epiphany sentences (e.g. 'Wait, I've verified my answer. No need to continue thinking.') and terminates without external signals (~50% early-termination rate on AIME), an emergent self-regulation behavior


### Memory mechanism

- **memory type**: none (no external memory store; the regulation is parametric — internalized in weights — not stored as episodic memory or a skill library)

- **memory persistence**: cross-task (the learned braking behavior is permanently in the fine-tuned weights and applies across all subsequent math-reasoning queries); not a runtime memory mechanism

- **memory curation mechanism**:

> n/a (no runtime memory to curate; the analogous offline 'curation' is the SBT data-construction pipeline that prunes redundant Evolution Solutions and applies loss masking to a small retained 'braking' segment so overthinking is exposed but not reinforced)


### Reflection granularity & timing

- **error localization granularity**:

> step-level (overthinking is detected at the level of reasoning steps/solutions — the transition from the Foundation Solution to redundant Evolution Solutions; SBT-D recomputes the overthink score after each step. The paper explicitly shows step-level detection beats token-level: AIME 14.17% vs 11.34% accuracy with fewer tokens)

- **intra task vs inter task**:

> intra-task (the braking corrects/truncates reasoning within a single problem-solving trajectory; there is no cross-task experience transfer or episodic carryover — the only cross-task element is that the behavior generalizes once trained into weights)

- **failure recovery vs avoidance**: mid-trajectory-recovery (the model learns to detect overthinking in-flight and terminate the redundant portion of the current reasoning chain at an appropriate braking point, rather than retrying in a future episode)


### Application domain

- **task domains**: math (mathematical reasoning only)

- **benchmarks**: GSM8K, MATH500, AMC23, AIME (AIME24 + AIME25); base/backbone models DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B (analysis), Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct


### Evaluation results

- **headline result**:

> Reduces token consumption by 30%-60% (up to ~62.8%) while preserving comparable accuracy. E.g. Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct: SBT-E cuts tokens 30.7% with only 2.65% accuracy drop, SBT-D cuts 23.0% with 1.95% drop; Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct: SBT-E cuts tokens 62.8% while preserving 94.1% of baseline accuracy. SBT-E averages 48.3% token reduction across models, SBT-D 43.9%.

- **baselines**:

> Models SFT'd on the unmodified OpenR1-Math dataset (same 92K instances, 16K context, no SBT truncation) serving as the unconstrained baseline; internal ablations vs token-level detection, vs special-token guidance, vs no-guidance, and vs removing the Masked Redundant Thinking (MRT) segment

- **gains vs baseline**:

> Versus the OpenR1-Math SFT baseline, SBT achieves 30%-60% fewer inference tokens with minimal accuracy loss. Best SBT-E config (threshold 0.2, beta 0.1, preserve 2 solutions + mask a few sentences) reaches 57.83% average accuracy at 1673 tokens vs baseline 59.36% accuracy at 3277 tokens — i.e. ~49% fewer tokens while retaining 97.4% of baseline accuracy. SBT-D can even improve MATH500 accuracy on Llama-3.1-8B by +2.62% while cutting tokens 58.7%.

- **compute cost profile**:

> Inference token cost reduced 0.4x-0.7x of baseline (30%-60% reduction; up to 62.8%); fewer generated tokens per query. Training cost: one round of SFT on ~92K examples per dataset (SBT-E or SBT-D), comparable to ordinary SFT — no RL rollouts or reward-model training. Data construction is an offline pass over OpenR1-Math trajectories.


### Limitations & critique

- **known limitations**:

> (1) Domain generalization: validated only on math reasoning; applicability to open-ended, commonsense, logical, or multimodal reasoning is unverified. (2) Data scalability/adaptivity: experiments limited to ~92K examples; scaling to millions untested; SBT-E/D rely on fixed thresholds that may need manual tuning per task. (3) Overthinking-signal definition: efficiency ratio + marker ratio may miss subtle/latent reasoning utility (seemingly redundant steps may serve hidden organizing purposes). (4) Interpretability/controllability: the internal termination decision remains opaque, with no explicit trace/control mechanism. (5) Complex-task trade-offs: for deep multi-step tasks (e.g. theorem proving) premature termination risks omitting critical steps.

- **oracle or external feedback dependency**:

> oracle-label/ground-truth (the overthinking-identification pipeline that builds the training data depends on standard/correct answers to compute the reasoning efficiency ratio — i.e. ground-truth labels are needed to locate braking points during data construction). However, the deployed model performs intrinsic-only self-braking at inference with no external feedback, tools, or oracle.

- **self correction efficacy**:

> task-dependent / net-positive for efficiency (consistently cuts tokens 30-60% with comparable or near-equal accuracy on math; SBT-D occasionally improves accuracy by removing harmful overthinking, e.g. +2.62% on MATH500 for Llama-3.1-8B). Math-specialized models gain less (more efficient already); general-purpose models gain more. Note the 'self-correction' here is redundancy-removal, validated against ground-truth during data construction.

- **calibration effect**:

> not-measured (the paper reports accuracy and token counts but does not directly measure confidence calibration / overconfidence; it argues a large fraction of LRM reasoning is genuinely redundant and removable without accuracy loss, but provides no calibration analysis)


### Failure analysis

- **failure attribution capability**:

> attributes-failing-step (the overthinking-identification framework localizes where in the reasoning trajectory the model transitions from effective reasoning — Foundation Solution plus useful Evolution Solutions — to redundant computation, i.e. pinpoints the redundant steps; it does not build a general failure taxonomy or attribute across agents)

- **failure mode addressed**:

> overthinking / redundant reasoning in large reasoning models (LRMs generate excessive Evolution Solutions and continue reasoning long after deriving the correct answer); cross-links to MAST-style 'overthinking' and to the broader 'reasoning tax' / redundant self-reflection failure mode. Does not target underthinking or premature termination (it explicitly guards against cutting too early via masking and preserving 2 solutions).

- **dataset or benchmark released**:

> Yes — two SFT datasets released: OpenR1-Math-SBT-E and OpenR1-Math-SBT-D (each 92,064 adaptive-reasoning-length examples), plus code and trained self-braking models via the GitHub repo (ZJU-REAL/Self-Braking-Tuning) and project page


### Relations

- **builds on**:

> DeepSeek-R1 / OpenAI o1-style large reasoning models; the OpenR1-Math reasoning-trajectory dataset (HuggingFace Open-R1); Qwen2.5-Math-Instruct and Llama-3 instruct backbones; the broader overthinking-mitigation literature it categorizes (RL length-reward methods, variable-length-CoT SFT, LightThinker, DEER, NoThinking, Token-Budget, Chain-of-Draft (CoD))

- **citation count**: 20 (Semantic Scholar, CorpusId 278769932, as of mid-2025; referenceCount 50)


### Other / reserved fields

- **reasoning model native**:

> yes (the method specifically targets R1/o1-style large reasoning models with built-in long-CoT reflection; it is built on and evaluated with DeepSeek-R1-Distill and reasoning-tuned Qwen/Llama models, and addresses the overthinking that is native to such reasoning models)

- **on policy distillation link**:

> Related but distinct: SBT is offline SFT on curated adaptive-length trajectories derived from a stronger reasoning model's outputs (OpenR1-Math, i.e. DeepSeek-R1 distillation data) with overthinking pruned — it is a length/skill-optimization via static-data distillation rather than on-policy distillation; no on-policy sampling or online teacher is used.

- **sample efficiency**:

> Single SFT pass on ~92,064 curated examples per variant (SBT-E or SBT-D) suffices to induce the self-braking behavior; no iterative/multi-trial optimization. Best operating point identified at overthinking threshold 0.2 (labels ~60% of samples as overthinking), beta=0.1, preserving 2 solutions plus a small masked braking segment.
